## Update 114 (2026-09-11, continued): candidate (a) -- no factory/allocation site for the renderer class (vtable 0x5696D8) found anywhere in the retail binary; a real, independent disassembly bug found along the way (dropped call at 0x002E7A6D-0x002E7B04)

**Task (user):** narrowly scoped, hypothesis-driven -- mechanically
analyze constructors `sub_002E7381`/`sub_002E7AC6` (object size,
vtable offset, RTTI), then search for the allocation/factory site
(direct calls, address-taken references, registration tables). No
blind grepping, no artificial construction, no fake vtable.

**Step 1 -- mechanical analysis of `sub_002E7381` (528 bytes, 162
insns):** writes `MEM32(esi) = 0x5696D8` (vtable pointer at object
offset 0), then `MEM32(esi+0x2C) = 0x500BBC` (a second vtable pointer
for a sub-object/base class at offset +0x2C -- suggests multiple
inheritance or an embedded sub-object), followed by extensive field
initialization up to at least object offset `0x7A58` (last observed
zero-fill loop: `edi = esi + 0x7A20`, 14 dwords). **Object size thus
lower-bounded at roughly 0x7A58 (~31,320 bytes)** -- no RTTI/
TypeDescriptor pattern (`??_R0`-style references) found in the
examined range. Afterward, several calls through a singleton manager
at `MEM32(0x5EAE74)` with constants `0x5696B8`/`0x569688` (sitting
immediately NEXT TO the class's own vtable at `0x5696D8` -- likely
metadata/parameter blocks of the same class, not RTTI).

**Step 2 -- searching for the allocation/factory site:**

- Direct calls (`RECOMP_ABI_CALL`) to `0x2E7381`/`0x2E7AC6` across
  ALL generated code (28,121 functions): **0**.
- Address-as-data references (raw XBE bytes searched for
  `struct.pack('<I', addr)`, whole image): **0** for both addresses.
- Raw byte scan of every executable section for each `E8` opcode
  (direct `call rel32`), target computed and compared against both
  constructor addresses (bypasses any possible bug in our own
  function-boundary detection entirely): `sub_002E7381`: 0 hits.
  `sub_002E7AC6`: **1 hit** at `0x002E7AA4`.

**That one hit led to a real, independent finding:** `0x002E7AA4`
lies INSIDE the function range our pipeline declared as
`sub_002E7A6D` (`0x002E7A6D-0x002E7AC6`, metadata says "89 bytes, 31
insns"). Re-disassembling `0x002E7A6D-0x002E7AE0` with capstone shows
this is actually AT LEAST THREE separate functions: (1)
`0x2E7A6D-0x2E7A90` (null check + helper call, ends `ret 8`), (2)
`0x2E7A93-0x2E7AA0` (null check + tail jmp `sub_002E7381`, ends
`ret`), (3) `0x2E7AA1-0x2E7AC3` (`push esi; mov esi,ecx; call
0x2E7AC6; ...; ret 4`) -- a "vector/scalar deleting destructor"-like
wrapper method. **Our generated C function `sub_002E7A6D` drops
function (3) entirely: the generated code jumps straight from
`loc_002E7AA0: esp+=4; return;` to `RECOMP_TRACE_PC(0x002E7AA9u)`,
completely skipping the 8 bytes at `0x2E7AA1-0x2E7AA8` (`push esi;
mov esi,ecx; call 0x2E7AC6`) -- the call simply does not exist in the
generated code, AND `esi` is used afterward (`PUSH32(esp, esi)` at
`loc_002E7AB0`) without ever being assigned.** This is the same bug
class as the `sub_0004023A` function-boundary bug fixed in commit
`6fbc129` -- undiscovered here until now because this code path is
never reached anyway (see below).

**Is this dropped call a new, external entry point into the renderer
chain?** No -- checking further shows the address `0x2E7AA1` (the
start of the dropped wrapper function) itself appears as a raw data
value exactly once, at VA `0x5696E4` -- that's slot `vtable+0xC`
INSIDE the very same vtable (`0x5696D8`) already confirmed never
installed (Updates 110/113). So this lead is circular: the dropped
call is itself only reachable via virtual dispatch on the same,
never-instantiated object -- not an independent external caller.

**Result:** across all four search methods (direct call, tail jump,
data literal, raw E8 byte scan), the ENTIRE retail binary contains
**no single external, independent caller/allocation/factory site**
for this vtable class's constructors. The only reference found is
internal (one vtable method pointing to another method of the same,
never-activated vtable). Object size (~31KB+) and vtable layout
suggest a real, substantial engine class (not a dead-code/debug
artifact based on size alone), but with no reachable caller it
remains open whether this class is ever instantiated at runtime in
the original game at all, or whether its activation depends on a
purely dynamic mechanism (e.g. a computed function pointer from a
runtime table, not a static literal).

**Separate, independently actionable finding:** the dropped-call bug
at `0x002E7A6D-0x002E7B04` is a real correctness defect in our
disassembly/function-boundary detection, INDEPENDENT of the
CreateDevice blocker (same class as `6fbc129`). Since the affected
code path isn't currently live-reached, fixing it has no immediate
effect on boot behavior, but it's relevant to codebase correctness
and should be fixed separately when convenient (ideally after
checking whether this is a one-off or a symptom of a broader
boundary-detection weakness).

**This closes candidate (a) from Update 110, within the narrow,
mechanical methodology requested (no RTTI/class-recovery project),
with no usable reference found.** Both (a) and (b) end at the same

## Update 115 (2026-09-11, continued): function-boundary bug root-caused -- NOT a generic disasm-engine defect, but a gap in the curated seed list; 23 addresses mechanically verified and added, full pipeline re-run

**Task (user):** close the renderer-vtable search path for now;
instead root-cause the `sub_002E7A6D` function-boundary bug: why does
function discovery mis-detect this boundary, generic fix if
reproducible, otherwise a minimal seed/override.

**Root cause found:** `tools/recomp/translator.py`'s
`FunctionTranslator` loads function boundaries EXCLUSIVELY from the
disasm output (`func_db`, from `tools/disasm`); `identified_functions.json`
(`func_id`) is used only for classification (`classification_db`),
NEVER for boundaries. This is **not a bug but deliberate, already
documented project policy** (see `docs/SCDA_WORKLOG.md`, around line
15560): `identified_functions.json` "is inference, not measurement"
and is therefore deliberately NOT passed as `--seed-functions` to
`disasm` -- precisely because of the historical Half-Life 2 case
(`0x00202C2E`, six bytes into a `mov`, caused a 250-caller frame
leak). The disasm engine's own seed mechanism (`--seed-functions`)
and its `instruction_covering()` safeguard were traced byte-by-byte
and are CORRECTLY implemented: a seed landing exactly on a clean
instruction boundary (not mid-instruction) is correctly accepted as
`seed_vtable_thunk` and correctly clips the surrounding function.

**Actual gap:** the curated, hand-verified seed list
`projects/scda/function_seeds.json` (1,466 entries) simply didn't
contain `sub_002E7AA1` yet -- `func_id`'s `vtable_thunk` heuristic had
already found this address (vtable `0x5696D8`, slot 3), but nobody
had promoted it into the curated list.

**Mechanical verification before adoption (no blind import):**
cross-referencing every `func_id` `vtable_thunk` entry against disasm
function boundaries shows **5,692 "swallowed" addresses across the
ENTIRE binary** (far too broad a scope for this round) -- narrowed to
the renderer range `0x2E2000`-`0x2E8000`: **25 candidates**. Each one
was individually verified via a capstone linear disassembly sweep
starting from its own already-confirmed owner function's real start
(more robust than a backward byte window, which produced 2 false
negatives on the first attempt). Result: **23 of 24 unambiguously
confirmed as real, clean function boundaries** (immediately after a
`ret`/unconditional `jmp` with no fallthrough); **exactly 1
(`0x002E798A`) exposed as a genuine false positive** -- it lands
mid-instruction inside `inc dword ptr [ebp-4]` (`FF 45 FC`), exactly
the failure mode the project's policy warns against. That one
candidate was NOT adopted.

**Fix:** added the 23 verified addresses to
`projects/scda/function_seeds.json`, each documented with its vtable
address, slot index, and verification method.

**Full pipeline re-run:**
1. `tools.disasm` re-run (56s): function count 28,113 -> **28,146**
   (+33, cascading effects from correctly re-bounded neighbor
   functions). `sub_002E7A6D` now correctly ends at `0x2E7AA1`;
   `sub_002E7AA1` now exists as its own function (`seed_vtable_thunk`).
2. `tools.func_id` re-run (8.0s): 33,815 total entries, 5,669
   `vtable_thunk` methods (essentially unchanged, as expected -- the
   fix affects disasm boundaries, not func_id's own, independent
   heuristic).
3. `tools.recomp` re-run (41.1s): 28,145/28,146 functions translated,
   0 failed.
4. Canonical build (`scda_recomp` target) succeeded. Timestamp
   `2026-09-11 22:47:17`, SHA-256
   `94F38E7605EB7A79206E5F95F9FDE5DD45A7A7D337954ED3A26ACACA7751C9C9`.

**Reachability re-check:** cdb probe (established pattern) on
`sub_002E75CE`, `sub_002E2BB1`, `sub_0049D210` -- still **0 hits**, as
already predicted in Update 114 (the fix only restores internal
reachability of ONE vtable method via virtual dispatch on the same,
still-never-instantiated object -- it doesn't change the external
instantiation question at all).

**Regression test:** 10-run batch: 9/10 `exit=124` (normal timeout),
1x (run 2) `exit=-1` -- a pattern never documented anywhere in this
project's history before. Since the script only sets `$rc=124` on the
timeout branch and reads `$rc=$p.ExitCode` only on a genuine
self-exit within 30s, this is a real, earlier self-termination with
exit code `-1`, not a script artifact. Investigated directly:

- Cross-checked against `PROJECT_STATUS.md`/`docs/SCDA_WORKLOG.md`:
  **zero prior occurrences** of `exit=-1` across dozens of documented
  regression/soak runs on every earlier build.
- Targeted repro attempt: 15 further runs on the same
  (function-boundary-fix) build, saving a log on every self-exit --
  **0/15 reproductions**, all 15 `exit=124`.

**Assessment:** 1 occurrence out of 25 runs on this build now, 0
occurrences across dozens of runs on every earlier build, 0/15 on a
targeted repro attempt -- this is **not solid evidence of a regression
caused by the function-boundary fix**, but it is also **not fully
explained or reproduced**. Documented honestly as open/unresolved
rather than dismissed as benign. Per standing policy (soak/survival
track CLOSED FOR NOW, no blind reliability hunting absent concrete
misbehavior), this single observation is not chased further unless it
recurs.

**Overall Update 115 result:** the function-boundary bug is
root-caused and fixed (no generic code fix needed, the seed mechanism
was already correct; 23 mechanically verified addresses added, 1
genuine false positive correctly rejected). Full pipeline + canonical
build succeeded, no new `[ABI]` corruption across 25 runs.
Reachability of `sub_002E75CE`/`sub_002E2BB1`/`sub_0049D210` remains
unchanged at 0 hits (expected, per Update 114 -- the fix only affects
internal vtable methods of the same, still-never-instantiated class).
The renderer-vtable search path stays CLOSED FOR NOW as instructed.

**Task (user):** close the renderer vtable/factory search (0x5696D8,
sub_002E7381, sub_002E7AC6) for now. New focus: not "how is THIS
object constructed" but "which higher-level engine/subsystem init
would even have to activate the renderer/video branch" -- outside-in
from startup/engine init through subsystem registration to the
renderer factory, not from the object back outward again.

**Starting point:** already documented in Update 109 but not yet
followed up: `sub_0004934E`'s first 229 instructions are an
**unconditional** chain of 229 direct calls ("class/subsystem
registration", 0 conditional branches in between) -- and
`sub_0004934E` itself is already confirmed live-reached. This means
**all 229 registration calls are guaranteed to run on the current,
stable boot path.**

**Structure of the 229 calls (capstone-verified):** each is an
identically-shaped "Meyers singleton" wrapper (`if (!guard) { guard =
Create(param); Register(guard); } return guard;`), 228 distinct
static guard variables, all targets densely packed in the
`0x39EAB`-`0x3E4EB` range. `func_id` categorizes essentially all 229
as `unknown` (too small/generic for its heuristics).

**The decisive hit:** the 229th (last) wrapper, `sub_000365DF` (call
site at `0x000497C2`, right at the end of the unconditional prefix),
internally calls **`sub_002E7B04`** and **`sub_002E2FA7`** -- BOTH
inside the renderer address range `0x2E2000`-`0x2E8000`! Cross-
referencing all 229 wrappers' inner calls showed this is the ONLY one
of the 229 whose inner calls land directly in that range.

**`sub_002E7B04`** (already a correctly-detected, standalone function
with a real prologue even before the function-boundary fix -- no
boundary bug here): allocates a 0xEC-byte object via the generic
allocator (`MEM32(0x5B57F8)`, the same allocator manager documented
elsewhere) and, if the allocation succeeds, calls **`sub_00066B0B`**
with 13 parameters, including the VALUE **`0x2E7A93`** and `0x4528E7`.

**`0x2E7A93` is the small dispatcher function already known from
Update 114** (`mov ecx,[esp+4]; test ecx,ecx; je +0x7; jmp
sub_002E7381; ret`) -- on a non-null `ecx`, a tail jump directly into
the known renderer constructor `sub_002E7381`.

**`sub_00066B0B` itself** is a generic "InitClassDescriptor" function:
writes `MEM32(this) = 0x4FE948` (a DIFFERENT, generic descriptor
vtable, not 0x5696D8), sets various flags/fields -- and writes
`0x2E7A93` UNCHANGED as a plain data value at object offset `+0xB0`
(a constructor-callback field), not as an immediate call. `0x4528E7`
lands at `+0xB4`.

**Is this renderer-specific?** No -- `sub_00066B0B` is called from
**554 sites** across the entire generated code. This is a generic,
engine-wide class registration system (a RenderWare-/MFC-CRuntimeClass-
style pattern: name/size/constructor-callback per class), not a
renderer-specific structure.

**Where is the `+0xB0` callback actually invoked?** All 20 methods of
the descriptor vtable `0x4FE948` itself were fully disassembled
(capstone) -- **none reads or calls `+0xB0`**. The invocation must
therefore come from an EXTERNAL manager/factory class holding a list
of such descriptors (offset `+0xB0` is read/written/indirectly called
at 15+ other sites across the generated code, but the offset is too
generic/widely reused to attribute without type tracking).

**Consumers of the renderer descriptor itself identified:** the
descriptor getter `sub_000365DF` has exactly **3 real callers** across
the ENTIRE code (fully statically enumerated):
1. the registration itself (`sub_0004934E`, already confirmed live).
2. `sub_00036DAD` -- a generic "IsKindOf(obj, descriptor)" type check
   (calls `sub_00036D4A` for the actual comparison; the descriptor is
   used only for comparison here, not instantiation).
3. `sub_000370E0` -- a generic "force registration, return the
   original pointer" pass-through (uses the descriptor only as a
   lazy-init side-effect trigger, not for instantiation).

**None of these 3 callers activates the `+0xB0` callback.** The next
needed piece of evidence (whether `sub_00036DAD`/`sub_000370E0` are
ever actually called WITH the renderer descriptor as an argument, and
whether any path from there reaches a generic "create instance of
type X" function) is not yet established -- but the space of possible
paths is now narrowed to these 2 generic consumer functions instead
of the entire call graph.

**Assessment against the requested outside-in methodology:** a
concrete, byte-verified, higher-level registration point was found and
confirmed live-reached. The chain from startup to subsystem
registration is now fully proven down to the descriptor level. The
next break sits between "descriptor registered" and "descriptor
actually used to create an object" -- a generic, class-wide mechanism
(not renderer-specific) whose concrete trigger (likely a scene/level/
config-driven "CreateObjectByType(name)" dispatcher) has not yet been
located.

**Next step (not yet executed):** check whether `sub_00036DAD`
(IsKindOf) or `sub_000370E0` (force-register) are themselves ever
called with the renderer descriptor as an argument (statically: who
calls THEM, and with what `esi` value?), and/or identify the generic

that object creation depends on game content/level data not yet
loaded at the current boot stage -- not a recomp bug, but a "not there
yet" state.

## Update 119 (2026-09-12): direct xemu ground-truth comparison -- Case A confirmed (a real device exists on hardware, a genuine boot-order divergence), the writer chain matches the Update-110 hypothesis exactly, and the precise break point in recomp is mechanically pinned down to a NULL factory result

**Task (user):** a targeted live xemu-vs-recomp comparison exactly at
the entry of `sub_0049CE00`. Three possible outcomes were specified
(A: xemu has a valid device there -> find the writer; B: xemu also
sees null -> our device assumption is wrong; C: xemu never reaches
that point -> the divergence is earlier). On Case A: identify the
writer, check the original bytes, then continue autonomously into the
recomp-side path without waiting for further confirmation.

**Method:** `xemu.exe -s -S` (halted at reset), talking the GDB remote
protocol directly over a Python socket (inline in each test run,
following the same approach already present but unused/uncommitted in
`tools/debug/xemu_0049ce00_check.py` and `xemu_4ab668_*.py` from an
earlier session).

**Case A confirmed immediately, on the very first test:** a breakpoint
exactly on `sub_0049CE00`'s entry, fresh boot: hit at `t=1.6s`,
`MEM32(0x004AB668) = 0x004AB670` (NOT null!), `ebx` holds the same
value directly (an object pointer), `eax = MEM32(dev) = 0x83934A7C`
(a valid guest heap address as the first field/vtable). On real
hardware a device object already exists by this point -- the
divergence is real and lies before this point.

**Writer identified (a clean write-watchpoint on `0x4AB668`, fresh
boot from reset):** exactly ONE write over the entire boot, at
`t=1.52s`, `EIP=0x0049D259` -- inside **`sub_0049D210`** (offset
+0x49), writing `MEM32(0x4AB668) = 0x004AB670`. The stack's return
address is `0x002E2BD2` -- inside **`sub_002E2BB1`**. This confirms,
directly via hardware ground truth, the exact chain `sub_002E75CE ->
sub_002E2BB1 -> sub_0049D210` that Update 110 had already identified
purely from static analysis as the "most plausible renderer-class
chain" but couldn't confirm live at the time -- not a false lead, but
the real CreateDevice path.

**Important methodology finding (side discovery):** an attempt to
determine call order by breakpointing `sub_002E75CE`, `sub_002E2BB1`,
`sub_0049D210`, and `sub_0049CE00` all at once in a single run failed
reproducibly: `sub_002E75CE` is a VERY hot path (several thousand
calls per second, apparently per object/scene node, not just per
frame), and the repeated stopping (GDB round-trip overhead per hit)
distorts the real time base so badly that the actual device creation
inside `sub_0049D210` (apparently gated by a condition that, under a
distorted wall-clock, never gets satisfied) never occurred in any of
these runs (up to 16,000 hits / 45s without a single creation). The
clean, minimally invasive single-breakpoint test (no hot-loop
breakpoint, only the actual target point) remained the only reliable
method and was used for every subsequent step.

**Caller of `sub_002E75CE` found (single-hit test, minimally
invasive):** `eax = 0x005696D8` on entry -- EXACTLY the vtable address
from Update 110/113-115! `ecx` (this) `= 0x008DDB30`. Return address
`0x00049819`, with the preceding bytes decoding byte-exact as `ff 50
68` = `call dword ptr [eax+0x68]` (a classic vtable dispatch), and
just before that `bf 80 02 00 00` = `mov edi, 0x280` (640 -- the same
default width value seen in `sub_00039A05`, Update 118!). **The caller
sits at absolute address `0x49816`, i.e. INSIDE `sub_0004934E`
itself** (function range `0x0004934E`-`0x0004A7A0`, confirmed via a
`functions.json` lookup) -- the SAME function already confirmed live
since Update 109/116 via its 229-call registration prefix, here hit at
a FURTHER point (offset `+0x4C8`, well past the registration prefix)
within the same function body.

**The generated C code fully confirms the context**
(`recomp_0002.c:17340`-`17368`): just before the vtable call, a
singleton/manager object is fetched (`call sub_001FA486` at `0x497F1`,
result stored to `MEM32(0x5E6DF8)`), then `eax = MEM32(ecx)` (the
vtable pointer reloaded), a push sequence `(1, 0x1E0, edi=0x280,
ebx)` -- a plausible `SetVideoMode(width=640, height=480, ...)`-style
call --, then `call dword ptr [eax+0x68]` -> `sub_002E75CE`.

**Live reachability test in recomp (canonical build, SHA
`94F38E76...`, cdb, source-line breakpoints via the `-G -logo` +
`-cf` script pattern, since plain stdout redirection hung buffered on
this build and only the `.bat` + `Start-Process` pattern reliably
delivered output):** **ALL THREE points along the call path are
reached** -- `recomp_0002.c:17339` (return from `sub_001FA486`),
`:17350` (vtable pointer reload), AND `:17359` (the icall point
itself) each fire exactly once. This finally overturns Update 110's
"not a single hit in 30s" for this chain -- explained exactly like the
cases already corrected in Update 118, by this session's intervening
fixes (heap lock, CPU affinity, function-boundary fix).

**Root cause of the break mechanically pinned down:** at the icall
point itself (`recomp_0002.c:17359`), recomp has **`eax = 0x0` and
`MEM32(0x5E6DF8) = 0x0`** -- instead of a valid vtable pointer
(`0x5696D8` on real hardware), the singleton/manager factory
(`sub_001FA486` -> `sub_000634DD`/`sub_000638CD`) returns **NULL**.
The subsequent icall computes `MEM32(eax+0x68) = MEM32(0x68)` --
reading garbage near address 0 instead of calling `sub_002E75CE`. An
additional breakpoint directly on `sub_002E75CE`'s entry confirms:
**the function is never entered in recomp at all.** This cleanly
explains the entire chain observed so far: the registration mechanism
(Update 116) runs correctly, the call site itself is reached (new,
overturning Update 110), but the generic object factory in between
returns NULL in recomp where it returns a valid renderer object on
real hardware -- and that is exactly what prevents the call to
`sub_002E75CE`, which in turn never reaches `sub_002E2BB1`/
`sub_0049D210` (the CreateDevice writer), which flows directly into
the Update 118 chain (`sub_0049CE00` stalling on the null device). A
single, precisely localized break point now explains the entire
investigated failure chain end to end.

**Still open (next step):** why does `sub_000634DD`/`sub_000638CD`
(the generic manager/singleton factory, addressed via a numeric
type/manager ID) return NULL in recomp? Candidates: (a) a missing or
faulty upstream registration for exactly this ID (similar to the
descriptor mechanism found in Update 116, but for a different, more
generic registry), (b) a genuine logic bug in `sub_000634DD` itself
(the function resembles an error/assert formatting path with several
conditional branches over `MEM32(0x5B5AC4)`/`MEM32(0x60123C)` -- not
yet byte-verified against the original XBE bytes), or (c) a parameter
passing error (the exact guest parameter values into
`sub_001FA486`/`sub_000634DD` could NOT be reliably read this round --
`@esp`/`dd`/`dwo(@esp+off)` do not resolve to valid guest memory
access in cdb for this build; only fixed absolute addresses and the
integer registers `eax/ecx/edx/ebx/esi/edi` read reliably; a different
approach for reading guest-stack parameter values is needed for the
next round, e.g. reading them from the caller side before the call
instead of from inside the callee). No live comparison of the exact
parameter values against xemu has been done yet.

**Verified:** xemu live tests (several fresh boot runs, breakpoint-
and write-watchpoint-based, GDB remote protocol via Python) and
recomp live tests (cdb, canonical build SHA `94F38E76...`, source-line
breakpoints); the call instruction at `0x2E2BCD`/`0x49816` decoded

## Update 120 (2026-09-12, continued): the NULL-factory cause narrowed down to an Unreal Engine config lookup ("Engine.Engine.RenderDevice"); the UMD extraction of the config file confirmed correct, config-cache resolution not yet byte-verified

context:** UTF-16, content **`"ini:Engine.Engine.RenderDevice"`**
(read via capstone/the XBE parser from `compare/orig/default.xbe`,
offset resolved correctly). The `"ini:"` prefix is a well-known
Unreal Engine 1/2 pattern (`FConfigCacheIni` default-property
substitution) -- `sub_0003B833` is therefore, with high confidence, a
generic **config value lookup** ("return the value of
`Engine.Engine.RenderDevice` from the ini configuration"), not object/
class factory code in the narrow sense.

configuration file:** `SplinterCell4Xbox.ini` (`[Engine.Engine]`

**The UMD extraction of this file in the current run is confirmed
working:** `scda_runtime.log` (current canonical build) shows exactly
**two** `[SCDA-UMD-READ]` entries with `len=3526`, whose content
preview `"[URL]..Protocol=unreal..ProtocolDescription=Unreal
Protocol..Nam"` matches BYTE-FOR-BYTE the start of the real
`SplinterCell4Xbox.ini` (the user-provided reference extraction). The

LOOSE files (`\Device\CdRom0\Default\SplinterCell4Xbox.ini` ->
`0xC0000034 FAILED`, three times, plus `SplinterCell4User.ini` the

**But: a very early symptom of the NULL result is already

at lines 663/680 -- not a timing/ordering cause) shows `[ICALL]
target 0x00000000 is not code -- skipped 1 time(s) ...
source=0x000497FD`. This is exactly the FIRST vtable dispatch right
after `sub_001FA486` returns (`recomp_0002.c:17346`, `MEM32(edx+0x64)`
with `edx = MEM32(eax)` -- if `eax` (the return value of

**Narrowing of the remaining break:** the ini file is read correctly

read" and "`sub_0003B833` returns the class-name string for

hash-cache sitting between them (the system already characterized on

## Update 121 (2026-09-12, continued): the call chain traced into genuine Unreal Engine object/reference parser code (`sub_00064DEF`); `sub_0003B833` corrected (a generic singleton getter, not ini-specific); a precise resume point marked for the next round

**Direct continuation of Update 120, via capstone against
`compare/orig/default.xbe`:**

**Correction:** contrary to the earlier guess, `sub_0003B833` is NOT
an ini-specific lookup -- it is a generic, parameterless singleton
getter (the Meyers-singleton pattern: `if (guard==0) { guard =
Constructor(0x4f56e0); Init(guard); } return guard;`), structurally
identical to the 229 wrapper functions from Update 109/116. The 5
values the caller pushes BEFORE this call (`ebx=0, 1, ebx=0,
0x4F7778, ebx=0`) are NOT its parameters (it takes none) -- they stay
on the stack and get forwarded together with the singleton's return
value (`eax`) as a 6-parameter call into **`sub_00065015`**:
`sub_00065015(manager=eax, 0, "ini:Engine.Engine.RenderDevice", 0, 1,
0)`. `sub_00065015` is therefore the actual lookup method on the
manager object `sub_0003B833` provides.

**`sub_00065015` disassembled:** builds a flag word (`param5 | 8`),
calls `sub_00064FF3(0, string, 0, flags)` -> result into `esi`; if
`esi == 0`, an immediate return path (return 0) with NO error
handling at all. Otherwise a vtable-method call follows (`call
[esi_vtable+...]` via `sub_0005FBAD`), and if that result is 0, a
log/report path (`sub_00070854`/`sub_000710DE` -- the same
formatting functions seen in `sub_000634DD`, Update 119, a recurring
generic error-reporting pattern throughout the engine code).
`sub_00064FF3` itself forwards all 5 parameters unchanged to
**`sub_00035CAC`** (one of the 229 calls already confirmed LIVE as
part of `sub_0004934E`'s own prefix -- presumably the global name/
string interning table manager) and calls **`sub_00064DEF`** with its
return value.

**`sub_00064DEF` identified as genuine Unreal Engine object-reference
parser code** (the pattern strongly matches `UObject::ParseObject`/
`StaticFindObject`-style logic): calls `sub_00062E2C` to split the
target string into name/package components; on a parse failure
(`test eax,eax; je ...`) the same generic error-report path follows
(`sub_00036EF5`/`sub_000710DE`/`sub_00070AEE`) and returns 0. On
success a longer chain of conditional object/package resolution
follows (`sub_000600ED`, `sub_000678C0`, `sub_00067F37`/
`sub_0067F84D` -- addresses approximate, `sub_0007F37F`,
`sub_0006321E`) with several fallback branches whose exact meaning
(which branch is taken for a not-yet-existing "package" like
`D3DDrv`) was NOT traced byte-exact this round.

**Assessment:** the call chain now concretely reaches into Unreal
Engine's generic object/class reference resolution code (no longer
SCDA-specific code, but core engine functionality -- matching exactly
the `FConfigCacheIni`/object-reference characterization already found
independently on 2026-09-02). The most plausible explanation for the
NULL result is that resolving the class name `D3DDrv.D3DRenderDevice`
(the `D3DDrv` PACKAGE, not just the ini value itself) fails at one of
these fallback branches -- e.g. because the `D3DDrv` package isn't yet
loaded/registered at this point in boot. That would be a GENUINE
boot-order difference (package load timing), not a pure string/ini
parsing bug -- exactly consistent with the entire Update 118/119/120
causal chain so far ("device-dependent code runs before its own
prerequisite").

**Precise resume point for the next round:** live-check via cdb which
branch inside `sub_00064DEF` (in particular the comparison at
`0x64E15`/`test eax,eax` after `sub_00062E2C`, and the comparison at

## Update 123 (2026-09-12, continued): the exact break point inside sub_0004721E mechanically proven -- a per-object field (`this+0x1C`) is not yet initialized at query time and overwrites the correctly-built string `"System.ini"` with an EMPTY global default

**Direct continuation of Update 122**, via a third, precisely isolated
diagnostic hook (a global `g_diag123_active` flag, set right around
the known icall inside `sub_00062E2C`, with `sub_0004721E` only
logging while the flag is set -- this isolates exactly ONE,
unambiguously identified call, instead of the ~750 calls/15s this
generic function receives engine-wide).

**Live result (canonical build, a single test run, the hook fully
reverted immediately after, a diff against the backup confirmed
byte-identical):**

```
[DIAG-4721E] ENTRY this=0x10ea7a8 param1(ebp+8)=0x4f56d0
             param2(ebp+c)=0x0 this+18=0x0 this+1c=0x0
             this+24=0x0 this+28=0x0
[DIAG-4721E] param1-str(ebp+8) = "System"
[DIAG-4721E] after-initial-copy(ebp-544) = "System"
[DIAG-4721E] FINAL-filename(ebp-544) = ""   <-- EMPTY!
[DIAG-62E2C-v2] GetString/Open call returned eax=0x0
```

`this=0x10ea7a8` unambiguously confirms the correct call (identical to
the `[SCDA-FILE-MANAGER-WRITE]` object from Update 122). All four
object fields (`+0x18`, `+0x1C`, `+0x24`, `+0x28`) are `0` at this
point -- a fresh, not-yet-populated state.

**Byte-exact tracing of the buffer's evolution between the two
measurement points (via capstone against `compare/orig/default.xbe`,
`0x00047265`-`0x00047412`) finds the exact turning point:**

1. Buffer = `"System"` (copied from `param1`, since `param1 != 0`).
2. Length (6) `>= 5` -> the short-form `jl` suffix-append path isn't
   taken directly; but since the buffer doesn't already end in `"."`,
   `".ini"` still gets appended unconditionally (`sub_00067872`) ->
   buffer = `"System.ini"`.
3. Compared against `"User.ini"` (`0x4F73CC`, via `sub_0006787C`):
   **no match** (as expected) -> proceeds to the next comparison.
4. Compared against `"System.ini"` (`0x4F73B4`): **MATCHES EXACTLY**
   (our buffer is already `"System.ini"`).
5. On a match: `cmp dword ptr [esi + 0x1C], ebx; je 0x473A3` --
   **`this+0x1C == 0`, so the jump is taken.**
6. At `0x473A3`: `eax = edi` (the register value from the function
   prologue, **`edi = 0x5A570C`** -- a global "default" pointer that
   is itself an EMPTY string, see Update 122). This value gets
   unconditionally copied BACK into the working buffer via
   `sub_00067886` (a string copy) -- **overwriting `"System.ini"`
   with an empty string.**

**Root cause named exactly:** the field `this+0x1C` on the
config-cache object (`0x10EA7A8`) is evidently meant as a cache for
the already-RESOLVED "System" ini file path (mirroring the
`this+0x18`/`this+0x1C` pair checked in the exact same way right at
the top of the function, for a completely different filename-type
combination). If this field is not yet populated (a fresh object, as
here), the code falls back to a GLOBAL, EMPTY default value instead of
simply using the `"System.ini"` string it just correctly built -- this
produces the observed empty-filename open attempt (six failed
`\Device\...\Default\` attempts, Update 122) and ultimately the NULL
return value propagating all the way up through `sub_0004934E`'s
vtable dispatch and the never-reached
`sub_002E75CE`/`sub_002E2BB1`/`sub_0049D210` CreateDevice chain.

**Precise next question (per the user's instruction: compare against
xemu only once the failure branch is known):** is `this+0x1C` (on the
equivalent config-cache object) already NON-NULL under xemu at this
point (e.g. a pointer to an already-resolved `"System.ini"` FString)?

and is that function even reached in recomp at all (if yes: why

## Update 125 (2026-09-12, continued): the next branching level identified (`MEM32(0x5B5800)`/`MEM32(0x5B57FC)`, two manager pointers for default-ini resolution); live values read on both platforms, recomp shows a suspicious identical value at both addresses

```
mov ecx, MEM32(0x5B5800)        ; primary manager pointer
cmp ecx, 0; je 0x4749A           ; if NULL -> fallback branch
  mov eax, MEM32(ecx); push &buffer; call [eax+0x10]   ; primary path
  ...
0x4749A (fallback, only if 0x5B5800==0):
  mov ecx, MEM32(0x5B57FC)      ; SECONDARY/default manager pointer
  mov eax, MEM32(ecx); push &buffer; call [eax+0x10]   ; the identical
                                                           call pattern on the other object
  test eax,eax; jl 0x474FC        ; on failure: COMPLETE ABORT (return NULL)
```

Both branches call the same vtable method `+0x10` on two DIFFERENT
manager objects -- presumably a "GetCommandLineOverride"/
"GetDefaultIniName"-style service, queried first from the PRIMARY
manager (`0x5B5800`, likely the active command-line/launch-parameter
context), falling back to a SECONDARY global default manager
(`0x5B57FC`) if that isn't set.

**xemu live check (breakpoint at `0x00047440`, 10 reproducible hits,
all identical):** `MEM32(0x5B5800) = 0xD00B1B90` (a valid, non-null
pointer) -- **the fallback branch at `0x4749A` is NEVER reached on

already present.

addresses):** `MEM32(0x5B5800) = 0x365AC4` and **`MEM32(0x5B57FC) =

only 4 bytes apart and logically supposed to be independent manager
pointers. `0x365AC4` also sits inside the address range of known CODE
sections (closer to `sub_000360E1`/`sub_00036xxx` than to any
plausible heap object) -- a strong hint of either (a) unpopulated/
uninitialized memory carrying a stale leftover value, or (b) a
genuine translation/initialization bug at this memory location. Since
the value is NOT null, recomp (like xemu) would take the PRIMARY
branch (`0x4744A`) -- but with a most-likely INVALID pointer as the
"manager" object, whose vtable dereference (`MEM32(ecx)`) and
subsequent icall (`[eax+0x10]`) would then quietly fail (via the
`RECOMP_ICALL_SAFE` fallback, no crash, but a most-likely wrong/empty
result).

## Update 126 (2026-09-12, continued): **Update 125 retracted** -- a `dwo()` measurement bug found and fixed; a clean live comparison shows the `0x5B5800`/`0x5B57FC` path behaves identically on both platforms (lead CLOSED); a new, deeper, verified finding: the real writer of the default-ini cache field is never reached in recomp

**A real methodology bug was found and fixed.** Update 125's cdb
command `dwo(0x5B5800)` was typed WITHOUT a `?` prefix, so cdb parsed
it as the command `dw` (Display Words) with the broken argument
`o(0x5B5800)` -- the reported "value" `0x365AC4` at both addresses
was never a real memory read, just an artifact of the failed command
parse. On top of that, correct reads of a fixed guest address must
account for `recomp_types.h`'s definition of
`MEM32(addr) = *(uint32_t*)((uintptr_t)(addr) + g_xbox_mem_offset)` --
a bare guest address is meaningless without adding this (run-dependent,
`0x10000` in this session) offset first, or a random host byte gets
read instead. The corrected techniques going forward: `? poi(ADDR +
poi(g_xbox_mem_offset))` for a fixed guest address, or -- more
reliably, whenever the generated code has already performed the
`MEM32()` read itself -- a breakpoint right after that line and `??
g_<register>` (the C++ evaluator; mandatory for the `RECOMP_TLS`
register globals `g_eax`, `g_ecx`, `g_edx`, `g_ebx`, `g_esi`,
`g_edi`, `g_esp` -- the plain `r` command and the bare `?` MASM
evaluator return only the identically-named HOST x64 register for
these names, not the TLS global; a second live-observed pitfall this
round).

**Re-test with the corrected methodology (recomp, cdb, `?? g_ecx`
right after `ecx = MEM32(0x5B5800);` at `recomp_0002.c:8257`):**
three hits give `0x10d78dc`, `0x10d7a4c`, `0x10d7a4c` -- **consistently
valid, plausible object pointers**, no trace of `0x365AC4` anywhere.
**Update 125 is hereby disproven and retracted; the
`0x5B5800`/`0x5B57FC` manager-pointer lead is CLOSED** -- it behaves
identically on both platforms.

**A full, clean re-comparison of the entire `sub_00048B15` init path**
(the writer of `0x5B5800`/`0x5B57FC`, see below):

- `MEM32(0x5ED140)`/`MEM32(0x5ED144)` at the decisive branch

## Update 127 (2026-09-12, continued): the Update 124 object identity is confirmed (not disproven); the real break narrowed down to a failing hash-table lookup (`sub_00046CE5`) -- recomp allocates a NEW entry on every single ini-key lookup instead of reusing the existing one

**A direct xemu test of the question Update 126 left open:** a
breakpoint at guest address `0x000472FE` (the equivalent of
`recomp_0002.c:7985`) gives `esi = 0x0081FC30` -- **exactly the same
object observed in Update 124.** The object-identity assumption from
Update 124 was therefore CORRECT, not unconfirmed as Update 126
suspected; `this+0x1C` (`0x0081FC4C`) is already populated with
`0x16` (22) at this point (t=1.473s) -- the write from Update 124
(t=1.327s) provably happened BEFORE this checkpoint, which is exactly
why a write watchpoint armed here never fires again.

**A direct xemu test of `sub_000464EC`'s calling context:** a
breakpoint right at the function entry (`0x000464EC`) gives, across
15 consecutive hits (t=1.356s through t=1.799s, roughly 32ms apart),
**the same value every time**: `ecx (this) = 0x0081BF48` -- and the
return address is `0x000474FC` in every case, i.e. **the exact same
caller recomp uses** (`loc_000474FC` inside `sub_0004721E`, the same
generic ini-key lookup from Update 126, no other/hidden call chain).
The caller is therefore NOT the divergence.

**The real difference sits one level higher:** `ecx` for
`sub_000464EC` comes from `esi = eax;` right after the preceding call
to `sub_00046CE5` (not, as first assumed, from `sub_00045FB0` --
that's just an intervening resource-release call with no effect on
`ecx`). `sub_00046CE5` was fully reconstructed via capstone against
`default.xbe`: it's a classic **hash-table lookup with find-or-create
semantics** -- bucket index via `(hash - 1) & capacity`, then walking
a chain (`loc_00046D03`/`loc_00046D15`) until an entry with a matching
key is found (`cmp MEM32(bucket+4), esi`) or the end-of-chain sentinel
(`0xFFFFFFFF`) is hit. On a HIT (`loc_00046D31`) it returns a pointer
to the EXISTING entry; on a MISS (`loc_00046D1C`) it calls
`sub_00046E1E` (insert/grow) and returns a freshly-created entry.

**On xemu:** all 15 observed consecutive calls (presumably 15
different keys/lines within the same section/file) pass the SAME
`this` (`0x0081BF48`) down to `sub_000464EC` -- meaning the hash-table
lookup in `sub_00046CE5` finds the SAME already-cached file/section
entry on every single one of these calls (correct find-behavior for
repeated access to the same ini section).

**In recomp (Update 126's numbers, revisited for comparison):** the 5
observed calls to `sub_000464EC` get 5 DIFFERENT `this` values
(`0x10d7980`, `0x10d7af0`, `0x10d7b14`, `0x10d7b38`, `0x10dccec`) --
meaning `sub_00046CE5`'s hash-table lookup MISSES on every single
call in recomp, allocating a brand-new entry each time instead of
finding the one inserted previously.

**New root-cause hypothesis:** recomp's config-cache hash table never
finds an already-existing entry again -- every ini-key lookup creates
a fresh, isolated entry. That would explain why the singleton-like
behavior (one central, reused cache per section) never materializes
in recomp, and specifically why `this+0x1C` on the actual singleton
object is never written (the write instead lands in one of the many
fresh, "orphaned" entries). Two possible explanations for the lookup
failure, not yet distinguished:
(a) the value passed in as `esi` (the key hash, `esi = MEM32(eax)`
    with `eax = MEM32(esp+4)`) differs between calls (e.g. because the
    hash is computed from a changing source -- a freshly-created
    FName/string per call -- instead of a stable, interned key), or
(b) the hash is stable, but the table itself (`edi`, `MEM32(edi)`,
    `MEM32(edi+0xC)`, `MEM32(edi+0x10)`) is not the same instance
    across calls (each call gets its own, empty table instead of the
    shared, already-populated one).

**Still open (the precise continuation for the next round):**
1. In recomp, put a breakpoint at `sub_00046CE5`'s entry
   (`0x00046CE5`) and log both `edi` (the table/"this") and `esi`

   consecutive calls -- determine whether (a) or (b) is the case.
2. Repeat the same test on xemu (at the same address `0x00046CE5`) to
   confirm both `edi` and `esi` stay constant across all 15 calls
   there.
3. Depending on the result: trace the origin of the key hash back
   (if (a)), or trace the origin/identity of the `edi` table pointer
   back (if (b)) -- in either case, down to the first point where
   recomp diverges from xemu.

**Verified:** measured live on both platforms (xemu via gdbstub, a
fresh boot per test; recomp's numbers from Update 126 reused and
compared directly against the new xemu numbers); `sub_00046CE5` fully
reconstructed via capstone against `default.xbe`; no source file

`0x000469AE`, INSIDE `sub_00046980` -- **this finally confirms Update

**Result 2 (confirms `sub_000464EC`/`0x4685D` as the next caller, BUT
with a decisive additional finding):** continuing to single-step until
`sub_00046980`'s OWN `ret 8` (step 222), EIP lands at `0x0004685D` --
exactly the address already suspected in Update 132 and (unsuccessfully)
searched for via breakpoint sampling in Update 137/138. **The caller
IS indeed `sub_000464EC`'s line at `0x4685D` -- but `sub_00046980`'s
"this" (register `esi`, preserved unchanged across the entire
`sub_000360E1` call via its own `push esi`/`pop esi`) is, for THIS
specific, actual write, `0x0081C614` -- NEITHER the singleton
(`0x0081FC30`) NOR the previously-observed "[URL]" section object
(`0x0081BFE8`), but a THIRD object.**

**The decisive break in the prior assumption:** this third object
(`0x0081C614`) has its OWN bucket array at `0x0081F440` (confirmed by
directly reading `[esi+0xC]` in the trace) and its OWN entries table,
which happened to be allocated at `0x0081FC40` -- **`0x0081FC40` sits
merely `0x10` bytes next to the singleton (`0x0081FC30`), which looks
numerically like "singleton+0x10", but is simply a neighboring,
completely independent allocation from the GENERIC pool allocator.**
The observed "write to singleton+0x18" (`0x0081FC48`) is therefore, in
reality, a write to `(independent object 0x0081C614)+0x18`, which
merely happens to sit at an address that numerically looks like a
singleton field.

**Consequence:** the ENTIRE causal chain built up since Update 122
("the ini-file-parser chain writes the loaded filename into a
singleton field") may have rested on confusing "an address numerically
close to the singleton" with "an actual field of the singleton".
**This chain is hereby fully retracted until it can be rebuilt on
object-identity-based (not address-based) proof.**

**What remains UNTOUCHED** (because it is independent of this
watchpoint-address issue): Update 122/124's original finding that
`MEM32(esi+0x1C)` INSIDE `sub_0004721E` (with `esi` proven, via the
complete icall/vtable chain, to be the real singleton) gives the value
`0x16` (22) remains valid -- that was a direct field access on an
object proven by call chain, not an address coincidence. **The actual
writer of THIS specific, still-genuine field is therefore once again
completely unknown**, and must be found using a method that doesn't
rely on "watchpoint a fixed address, then treat the first hit as
causal" -- since that exact approach has now provably produced a false
hit when a different, independent allocation happened to land at the
same or a neighboring address.

**An important new methodological rule for this project:** a write
watchpoint on a fixed address only proves that SOMETHING wrote there --
it does NOT prove that the writing object is the same object whose
address originally led to that value, unless object IDENTITY is
additionally confirmed through an independent channel (a vtable value,
a unique field pattern, call-chain proof). Plain address matching
(`base+offset`) is NOT sufficient with a generic pool allocator that
densely packs many small, short-lived objects next to each other.

**Still open (for the next round, with corrected methodology):**
1. Find an object-identity-safe way to observe the real writer of the
   singleton's `this+0x1C` -- e.g. by NOT keeping the watchpoint
   permanently armed on a fixed address, but only arming it once a
   one-time read has confirmed that the same object still occupies
   that address (e.g. by comparing a known, stable neighboring field
   such as a vtable pointer, if the singleton has one).
2. Alternatively: on every watchpoint hit, immediately (as demonstrated
   in this update) single-step back to the immediate caller and check
   ITS "this"/object identity directly, BEFORE treating the hit as
   relevant -- adopt this as a standard step for every future
   watchpoint-based root-cause search in this project.
3. Determine whether there is even a single, identifiable "writer" for
   the singleton field at all, or whether the value
   (`SplinterCell4Xbox.ini`, length 22) arrives there in a completely
   different way (e.g. a direct, hardcoded initialization at object
   construction, not via the ini-parser chain).

**Verified:** a fully single-step-based proof (no breakpoint-sampling
perturbation in this update -- every step individually confirmed); no
source file changes; all xemu processes were cleanly terminated at the
end.

## Update 140 (2026-09-13, continued): **THE REAL WRITER FOUND, ROOT CAUSE PROVEN, FIX IMPLEMENTED, BUILT, AND FUNCTIONALLY VERIFIED** -- a classic function-boundary/vtable-thunk bug (the same class as `sub_0004023A` and `sub_002E7A6D`/`sub_002E7AA1`) had been swallowing `sub_0004626E` all along

**Methodology (strictly per the rule set in Update 139: object
identity FIRST, address only afterward):**

1. The real singleton identified independently and early: a write
   watchpoint on the GLOBAL HANDLE `0x005EAE74` (not a guessed object
   address!) catches, at t=1.508s, the write `MEM32(0x5EAE74) =
   0x0081FC30`. Object identity confirmed IMMEDIATELY:
   `MEM32(0x0081FC30) = 0x004F7248` -- exactly the FileManager
   singleton's vtable, independently known since Update 122. Writer
   EIP `0x00071D7A` sits inside `sub_00071B49` -- the singleton's own
   constructor/factory function (satisfying the "constructor/factory
   origin" criterion).
2. Immediately after, on the NOW-proven object base, a second
   watchpoint armed on `0x0081FC30 + 0x1C` -- fires after only 1ms:
   writer EIP `0x000D2914` (`sub_000D28EC`), called with
   `ecx = 0x0081FC48` (= object base+0x18, an embedded FString field).
   The stack shows the return address `0x0004627D` and readable raw
   bytes `"Spli"` (the start of `"SplinterCell4Xbox.ini"`) right there
   on the stack.
3. `0x0004627D` sits inside `sub_00046248` (0x46248-0x4628D) -- but
   capstone shows: this is a SECOND, independent function
   (`push esi; push [esp+8]; mov esi,ecx; lea ecx,[esi+0x18]; call
   sub_D28EC; lea ecx,[esi+0x24]; call sub_D28EC; ret 0xC`) starting at
   `0x0004626E` -- IMMEDIATELY after `sub_00046248`'s own `ret 0x10` at
   `0x0004626B`. `sub_00071B49`'s construction sequence calls this
   function via `call [vtable+0x40]` (vtable already confirmed as
   `0x4F7248`) -- a REAL, independently-proven vtable dispatch chain,
   not an address coincidence.

**Root cause pinpointed beyond doubt:** `tools/disasm`'s
`tail_jump_alias` detection had incorrectly treated `sub_0004626E`'s
31 bytes (`0x0004626E`-`0x0004628D`) as a continuation of
`sub_00046248` (ending at `0x0004628D` instead of correctly at
`0x0004626E`). In the generated `recomp_0002.c`, this meant
`sub_0004626E`'s FIRST half (the `this+0x18` call) was MISSING
entirely, and the SECOND half (the `this+0x24` call, from
`loc_0004627D` onward) got stuck as dead code AFTER an unconditional
`return;` inside `sub_00046248` -- syntactically present but
UNREACHABLE with no jump target/label. The ICALL dispatch table
consequently had NO entry for `0x0004626E`; `recomp_lookup()`'s flat
table therefore resolved the vtable address `0x0004626E` to
`sub_00046248`'s host function, which instead executed from ITS OWN
start (`loc_00046248`) -- entirely different, unrelated logic that
never calls `sub_000D28EC` and never writes `this+0x18`/`this+0x1C`.
**Confirmed via `scda_runtime.log` line 7588 from an EARLIER canonical
run:** `[ICALL] source=0x00071D7F target=0x0004626E ...
eax=0x010EA7A8 ecx=0x010EA7A8` -- the icall itself already resolved
correctly to the RIGHT object before the fix was applied; the problem
lay exclusively in the missing function boundary, not in the icall
mechanism.

**This is exactly the same function-boundary-swallowing class already
documented twice in this project** (`sub_0004023A`, commit `6fbc129`;
`sub_002E7A6D`/`sub_002E7AA1` and 23 siblings, commit `55b219a`) --
func_id had already CORRECTLY identified `sub_0004626E` as a
`vtable_thunk` (`vtable_addr=0x004F7248`, `vtable_index=16` -- exactly
`[vtable+0x40]`, independently confirmed via live trace), but nobody
had promoted this finding into the verified seed list.

**Fix (smallest possible, generic, exactly matching the established
pattern):** a single new entry in `projects/scda/function_seeds.json`
for `0x0004626E`, with a detailed justification following the same
format as the 23 prior entries of this class. No change to
`tools/disasm`, `tools/func_id`, `tools/recomp`, or any generated/
hand-written code itself.

**The full pipeline re-run for real:**
1. `py -3 -m tools.disasm ... --seed-functions
   projects/scda/function_seeds.json --force -v` -- 57.5s;
   `sub_00046248` now correctly `0x00046248`-`0x0004626E` (38 bytes),
   `sub_0004626E` now its own function `0x0004626E`-`0x0004628D`
   (31 bytes, `detection_method: seed_vtable_thunk`); total function
   count 28146 -> 28147 (+1, exactly the expected single new split).
2. `py -3 -m tools.func_id ...` -- 8.0s, 33815 total functions,

3. `py -3 -m tools.recomp ... --all --split 1000 ...` -- 28147/28147

4. `cmake --build build/scda_upgrade --config RelWithDebInfo -j 8` --

   SHA-256
   `2fa55a90a43e577d2c6c52e0fc2e90693eced90b1285b232d982c90358e9a806`**
   (differs from the previous canonical build, as expected for a
   genuine pipeline regeneration).

**Functional verification (cdb, `recomp_0002.c:8006`, `esi` =
singleton `0x010EA7A8`):**
- `MEM32(esi+0x1C) = 0x16` (22) -- **exactly the xemu value from

**But:** the original symptom marker tracked since Update 119

**An important side finding (do NOT chase blindly):** a systematic

## Update 141 (2026-09-13, continued): **A SECOND, INDEPENDENT INSTANCE OF THE SAME BUG CLASS FOUND, ROOT CAUSE PROVEN, FIX IMPLEMENTED, BUILT, AND FUNCTIONALLY VERIFIED**

The task was to prove, beyond doubt, the real writer of the config-cache
singleton's `this+0x1C` field, with an explicit rule: address proximity alone
is never acceptable proof of object identity. Outcome: Update 140's fix
(`sub_0004626E`) was real and correct, but a COMPLETELY SEPARATE, independent
bug of the same class was still blocking the actual RenderDevice boot path.

**Methodology (as mandated): object identity first, then watchpoint.** No
candidate was accepted on address proximity alone -- every step was confirmed
via at least one of the required anchors (constructor origin, unique call
context, independent xref confirmation).

**Step 1 -- anchor, not address:** the call site `0x000497EC` inside
`sub_0004934E` (a direct `call sub_001FA486`, whose immediate next
instruction is exactly `0x000497FD` -- `call dword ptr [edx+0x64]`) was used
as an unambiguous anchor, free of the address-reuse trap that sank the first
attempt (a breakpoint on `sub_000634DD`'s function entry instead caught a
completely unrelated caller -- return address `0x00063B47` instead of the
expected `0x000638F4`, caught immediately via mismatched ESP values and
discarded).

**Step 2 -- live comparison of object construction, xemu vs. recomp, same
anchor:**
- Entry state into `sub_000634DD` for this exact call: `[P1+0x90]=0x401E`
  identical on both platforms, global flags `MEM32(0x60123C)=0` /
  `MEM32(0x5B5AC4)=1` identical, BOTH platforms take the same success path
  (return via `0x638C6`, not the NULL path `0x63645`). So `sub_000634DD`'s
  own branch logic is not the divergence source -- following the user's own
  rule: "if entry values match, the divergence is deeper."
- xemu produces a fully constructed object (`0x008ddb30`) with a valid vtable
  `0x005696D8`; recomp produces an object (`0x01199588`) with vtable `0`.
- Tracing the object backward through the full call chain
  (`sub_000634DD -> sub_0003EDBF -> sub_00077B38 -> sub_000774E6`) shows: the
  actual memory allocation (`sub_000774E6`, a generic pool allocator with
  free-list bookkeeping) installs no vtable at all -- expected, since pool
  allocators only hand back raw memory.
- A byte-verified, identity-anchored write watchpoint on
  `[freshly_allocated_object+0]` (armed immediately after the allocator
  returns, on xemu) caught the TRUE writer: `sub_0005F722` (3
  capstone-verified instructions: `mov eax,ecx; mov dword ptr [eax],
  0x4fdb70; ret`, `call_target`-detected with ~100 callers -- a generic
  base-class constructor stub). Write identity proven via `eax=ecx=esi=edi=
  object address` at the exact moment of the write.
- Tracing backward from the writer to its immediate caller:
  `sub_000638CD`'s CONDITIONAL `call dword ptr [esi + 0xB0]` (source
  `0x00063910`, reached only when `MEM32(0x5ED104)!=0` AND NOT
  `(MEM32(esi+0x92) & 0x40)`), where `esi` is the manager/type object
  threaded through the entire chain (`sub_0004934E -> sub_001FA486 ->
  sub_000638CD -> sub_000634DD`) -- identity confirmed via `[esi+0]=0x4FE948`
  (the same manager vtable at every level).
- `MEM32(esi+0xB0)` resolves IDENTICALLY on xemu and recomp: `0x002E7A93`.
  The dispatch resolution itself is correct on both platforms -- the bug is
  in recomp's TRANSLATION of that target address.

**Step 3 -- root cause:** `0x002E7A93` sits in the exact same bug class as
`sub_002E7A6D`/`sub_002E7AA1` (Update 115, 23 siblings already fixed) -- but
this one specific address was MISSED by that earlier fix. Capstone proof:
`sub_002E7A6D` cleanly terminates with `ret 8` at `0x2E7A90`; immediately
after, a genuinely separate, 14-byte dispatcher begins (`mov ecx,[esp+4];
test ecx,ecx; je 0x2E7AA0; jmp 0x2E7381; ret`) that tail-jumps into the
already-fixed constructor `sub_002E7381` (writes vtable `0x005696D8`).
Independently confirmed via `xrefs.json`: a `data_imm` xref from `0x002E7B2E`
to `0x002E7A93` proves this address is referenced as a function-pointer
constant in the code (not scanner noise).

Because this 14-byte function was never registered on its own, the flat
ICALL dispatch table maps `0x002E7A93` to `sub_002E7A6D`'s own host function
pointer, which instead starts executing from that function's own, unrelated
prologue (`xor eax,eax; cmp [0x6A8EB4],eax; ...`) -- `sub_002E7381`'s
constructor is never reached, and the object's vtable stays 0.

**Fix:** one new entry in `projects/scda/function_seeds.json` for
`0x002E7A93` (same format/methodology as the previous 24 entries of this bug
class).

**Pipeline actually run:** disasm (56.1s, 28148 functions, `sub_002E7A6D` now
correctly ends at `0x2E7A93`, `sub_002E7A93` now its own function) -> func_id
(7.9s) -> recomp (28148/28148 translated, 0 failed, `sub_002E7A93` now listed
as its own function in `recomp_dispatch.c`) -> `cmake --build` (exit code 0,
new build 2026-09-13 14:52, SHA-256
`7d674df4f10aa75fe6c67fcd614239bae62c855b0171d0cf374c4d6cdaa33b7b`).

**Functional verification via cdb:** at the same anchor (`0x000497EC`), the
final state now shows `eax=0x01199588`, `[eax+0]=0x005696D8` -- exactly
matching xemu's reference value, byte for byte. Fresh boot run: the old
symptom (`0xC00000BA`) stays at 0 occurrences; `source=0x000497FD` and
`source=0x00063910` no longer appear in the failure log at all (both ICALLs
now resolve correctly); boot progresses noticeably further (new next blocker
at call #180413/#180422, source `0x004C2530`/`0x004C2543`, versus
#175590/#177582 at `0x000497FD` before).

**Important note for the overall chronology:** the config-cache singleton
chain traced since Update 122 (Update 140's fix, `sub_0004626E`) was a REAL,
independent bug -- but NOT the cause of the RenderDevice-NULL symptom from
Update 119. The actual cause was, the whole time, this second, independent
vtable-installation bug in a completely different class. Both fixes were
necessary; neither alone would have been sufficient.

**Still open:** a new blocker at `source=0x004C2530`/`0x004C2543` (call
#180413/#180422) -- not yet investigated. Next step: apply the same
methodology (object identity first) to this new address.

**Verified:** the full pipeline was actually run and checked at every stage
(function-count deltas, generated code, dispatch table, build exit code,

as a changed tracked file; functional verification via cdb performed and

## Update 142 (2026-09-13, continued): **NOT A FUNCTION-BOUNDARY BUG THIS TIME -- MISSING INSTRUCTION EMULATION (`pushfd`/`popfd`/`cpuid`) FOUND AND FIXED GENERICALLY**

Task: isolate the new first blocker (`source=0x004C2530`/`0x004C2543`) without
jumping to a function-boundary-bug conclusion prematurely.

**Step 1 -- static analysis:** both addresses sit in `sub_004C2180` (BINK
section, `call_target`-detected, clean). They are two `call dword ptr
[GLOBAL]` sites (`[0x5EAE40]` and `[0x5EAE28]`), not per-object vtable
dispatches, but global function-pointer slots Bink uses to select its
copy/decode routines based on CPU features.

**Step 2 -- function-boundary check:** all six candidate functions that can be
written into these slots (`sub_004C1980`, `sub_004C1A40`, `sub_004C17E0`,
`sub_004C18B0`, `sub_004C1BE0`, `sub_004C1C20`) are already correctly
detected as their own functions (`indirect_call_slot`). No boundary bug here
-- so nothing was seeded on suspicion, per the user's explicit instruction.

**Step 3 -- xemu as ground truth:** a live breakpoint at `0x004C2530` shows
`[0x5EAE40]=0x004C6140` on xemu (valid, initialized) versus `0` on recomp --
not a harmless shared state, a genuine recomp regression.

**Step 4 -- tracing the initializer backward:** `sub_004C2180` calls
`sub_004C1CF0` (at `0x4C226E`) before using the slots. `sub_004C1CF0` calls
`sub_0005ED70` and then reads `[0x6B2790]`; if that value is 0, the ENTIRE
codepath that writes `[0x5EAE40]`/`[0x5EAE28]` (and several other slots) is
skipped.

**Root cause:** `sub_0005ED70` is a classic CPUID-availability probe with
caching: `pushfd; pop eax; xor eax,0x200000; push eax; popfd; pushfd; pop
eax; popfd; cmp eax,ebx` (toggle EFLAGS.ID and check if it stuck), followed
by a real `cpuid` call checking EDX bit 23 (MMX support). `pushfd`, `popfd`,
and `cpuid` were plain TODO placeholders (no-ops) in the code generator
(`tools/recomp/lifter.py`) -- confirmed both in the generated code and in
`summary.json`'s "unimplemented" list. As a result the toggle-and-compare
was comparing stale, unrelated register contents, and `cpuid` itself never
returned real values -- the result ("MMX unsupported") was effectively
random rather than correct, and consistently wrong in this particular run.

**Fix (generic, not SCDA-specific, since `pushfd`/`popfd`/`cpuid` are
missing for every recompiled Xbox title):**
1. `templates/runtime/recomp_types.h`: a new `RECOMP_TLS uint32_t g_eflags`
   (a synthetic EFLAGS backing store, starting value `0x00200202` with the
   ID bit set) and a declaration for `recomp_cpuid(leaf, subleaf,
   *eax,*ebx,*ecx,*edx)`.
2. `src/kernel/xbox_memory_layout.c`: defines `g_eflags` and implements
   `recomp_cpuid` via the real MSVC `__cpuidex` intrinsic (the host is
   x86-64, so it truthfully reports MMX/SSE/SSE2 -- a superset of the
   original Xbox's Coppermine-based CPU, so this never unlocks a codepath
   the original game didn't already expect on real hardware).
3. `tools/recomp/lifter.py`: `pushfd`/`popfd` now lift to `PUSH32(esp,
   g_eflags)`/`POP32(esp, g_eflags)`, `cpuid` to `recomp_cpuid(eax, ecx,
   &eax, &ebx, &ecx, &edx)`.

**A stumbling block along the way:** `tools/recomp/output/scda_v060/gen/recomp_types.h`
is, by pipeline policy, "never overwritten" (a project may edit its own
copy). The existing copy was stale and missing this AND an earlier generic
improvement. Since it showed no project-specific customization (only
missing newer generic content), it was deleted/replaced with the current
template (`cp -f`), exactly as the pipeline's own code comments recommend
("Delete it to get the current one back"). Also: a first build reported
"exit code 0" despite failing, because `| tail -60` swallowed `cmake
--build`'s real exit code -- a nested `/* TODO */` inside my own comment
text had closed the C comment early (C2059/C2018 errors). Fixed the comment
(no literal `/*`/`*/` pairs left in the prose), verified comment nesting
depth with a script (0 at end of file), then built cleanly (explicitly
checked the build log for 0 "error" hits rather than trusting the
misleading pipe exit code).

## Update 143 (2026-09-13, continued): **GENERIC ENGINE GAP CLOSED -- `--exclude-seed-functions` now also applies to disasm's OWN internal candidates, not just externally injected seeds; fixed a SEH-boundary bug in `sub_0003EDF3`**

Task: isolate the blocker at `source=0x0007F77F` (call #305036).

**Static analysis:** the address sits in `sub_0007F412` (cleanly detected,
`prologue`), a normal vtable dispatch (`call dword ptr [eax+0x60]`). The
runtime diagnostic (`[ABI] sub_0003EDF3: esi esp(epilogue never ran)`) showed
the real bug elsewhere: an ABI violation with `esi` clobbered to 0 and `esp`
off by -2076 bytes -- the classic signature of a C function that never
reaches its own epilogue.

**Root cause:** `sub_0003EDF3` is a real, 685-byte SEH `__try`/`__finally`
function (MSVC `_except_handler3` pattern: locals at `ebp-4`/`ebp-0xc`/
`ebp-0x10`, `mov dword ptr fs:[0], ecx` at the real epilogue). Its own
`__except` filter (addressed only as a data immediate, `mov eax, 0x3EE32`,
for the scope table) was detected by disasm's `imm_ref_target` pass as a
STANDALONE function (it decodes clean to a ret, so it looks like a real
function, but actually shares the `__try` function's stack frame and is
never independently callable). This made `sub_0003EDF3`'s own boundary
computation ("run to the next known function start") stop early at 63 bytes
instead of 685 -- mid-body, on a bare `call dword ptr [eax]` with no ret at
all.

**Why the existing exclude mechanism didn't help:** `--exclude-seed-functions`,
per `tools/disasm/__main__.py`, only ever filtered the externally supplied
`--seed-functions` list, before it even reached `FunctionDetector`. A
candidate found by one of disasm's OWN internal passes (here:
`imm_ref_target`) never passed through that filter at all -- even though the
flag's own help text ("proven false-positive vtable entries inside larger
functions") implied it should. A documentation/implementation mismatch.

**Fix (generic to the disassembler, not SCDA-specific):**
1. `tools/disasm/functions.py`: `FunctionDetector.__init__` gains a new
   `exclude_addrs` parameter; `_add_candidate` (the one shared choke point
   every detection pass funnels through: known_addresses, prologues,
   call_targets, indirect_call_slots, tail_jump_targets, imm_ref_targets,
   table_entries) now rejects candidates in that set.
2. `tools/disasm/disasm.py`: `Disassembler` threads a new
   `exclude_functions` parameter through to `FunctionDetector`.
3. `tools/disasm/__main__.py`: the already-loaded `excluded_seed_funcs` set
   is now also passed as `exclude_functions`, so the same curated exclude
   list covers both cases (externally seeded AND internally discovered
   false positives) from now on.
4. `projects/scda/function_seed_excludes.json`: two new entries, `0x0003EE32`
   (the SEH filter itself) and `0x0003EE3F` (the immediately following
   `mov eax, 0x3EE32; ret` fragment).

**Pipeline/build:** disasm confirms the fix immediately (`sub_0003EDF3` now
176 instead of 63 bytes, correctly ending at `0x3EEA3`; `sub_0003EE32`/
`sub_0003EE3F` no longer exist as their own functions; total 28148->28144).
func_id (8.1s) -> recomp (28144/28144 translated, 0 failed, `sub_0003EDF3`
now a single, coherent C function with a correct epilogue including the
`xbox_fs_write32(0, ecx)` restore and `ret 8`) -> `cmake --build` clean
(build log explicitly checked for 0 errors), new build 2026-09-13 16:42,
SHA-256 `a9b5c1997b26a9ba27f63711724c8d510c10a0ae4972a7e0a1eac91c6c7d1cca`.

**Functional verification:** the generated code for `sub_0003EDF3` was
checked against the capstone reference disassembly -- exact match (the SEH
filter block is now inline as `loc_0003EE32`, the dead code after it is
correctly unreachable). Fresh boot run: the old blocker (`source=0x0007F77F`)
no longer occurs; no immediate crash there anymore -- the process kept
running actively for over 5 minutes (had to be terminated manually) and
reached a much deeper, previously unexplored region of the game.

**New state (noticeably more tangled than a single blocker):** instead of
one clean next blocker, the log now shows several PARALLEL ABI violations
across different, not-yet-examined functions (`sub_00076402`,
`sub_0024493D`, `sub_001FA1BB`, `sub_00246CB4`, `sub_0026940F`), plus
repeated failed file opens (`0xC0000034`) for various virtual device paths
and a suspicious, recurring bad ICALL target value (`0x080A080A`, which
looks like uninitialized/garbage memory). This is a deliberate stopping
point: the confusion of several simultaneously visible symptoms at a
freshly-reached, unfamiliar code location calls for its own fresh
investigation round using the same object-identity methodology, rather than

**Still open:** the newly visible ABI violations and the `0x080A080A` bad
value are NOT investigated. Next step for the next round: isolate whichever
of these new symptoms comes first (chronologically/by call number) and apply
the same methodology (static analysis -> function-boundary check -> xemu as
ground truth -> root cause).

**Verified:** `git status` shows only `projects/scda/function_seed_excludes.json`,
`tools/disasm/__main__.py`, `tools/disasm/disasm.py`, and
`tools/disasm/functions.py` as changed tracked files; build log explicitly

## Update 144 (2026-09-15): Third Independent Instance of the Vtable-Thunk-Swallowing Family Found and Fixed (0x756ED / 0x74873)

**Starting point:** Update 143 had fixed the previous blocker (`source=0x0007F77F`) but left a cluster of new, simultaneously-visible symptoms at a freshly-reached code location undiagnosed (`sub_00076402`, `sub_0024493D`, `sub_001FA1BB`, `sub_00246CB4`, `sub_0026940F`, plus `0x080A080A` and `0x00000000` ICALL bad-target values). Task for this round: isolate whichever of these symptoms occurs earliest by call number and apply the same methodology (static analysis first -> function-boundary check -> xemu as ground truth -> smallest generic root cause).

**Chronological ordering:** in a fresh boot log, `[ABI] sub_00076402: ebx esi edi` is the earliest of the new symptoms, immediately followed by `[ABI] sub_0024493D: ebx esi edi` with an identical register delta -- `sub_0024493D` directly calls `sub_00076402` (confirmed via `calls_to`/`called_by` in `functions.json`), so the second report is a cascade of the first, not an independent second finding.

**Static analysis of `sub_00076402`:** Capstone disassembly of the original bytes against the generated code (`recomp_0003.c:47173`) shows a byte-exact, correct translation including a clean prologue/epilogue (`push ebx/edi/esi` .. `pop esi/edi/ebx/ebp; ret`). No function-boundary problem in this function itself. The last indirect-call line logged before the ABI violation was the useful lead: `[ICALL] source=0x00076636 target=0x000756ED` -- exactly the `call dword ptr [ebx+0xB0]` vtable dispatch site INSIDE `sub_00076402` itself (0x76636 in the original disassembly).

**Root cause:** `functions.json` had NO function at all covering 0x756ED. `sub_000756E5` (a 3-instruction destructor stub) correctly ends its own body exactly at 0x756ED, but the following 14 bytes belonged to no function. Capstone on `compare/orig/default.xbe` at 0x756ED confirms a byte-exact dispatcher: `mov ecx,[esp+4]; test ecx,ecx; je 0x756FA; jmp 0x74873; ret` -- the same mov-ecx/test/je/jmp/ret signature as the two Update 141 instances. `xrefs.json` confirms a `data_imm` xref from 0x0007613F to 0x000756ED (a vtable slot constant), matching the whole family's "only reached via a data pointer" signature.

This finding pulled in a second, equally invisible gap: the 0x756ED dispatcher tail-jumps to 0x74873, which itself was never detected as a function -- `sub_0007483E` (a destructor helper) correctly ends at 0x74873, but the following 22-byte destructor-like method (`push esi; mov esi,ecx; call 0x73CD0; and [esi+0x30],0; mov [esi],0x501298; mov eax,esi; pop esi; ret` at 0x74888) had no candidate either. Reason: `_pass_tail_jump_targets` only scans instructions inside already-known function bodies, and 0x756ED was not one, so its internal `jmp` was never seen.

**Fix:** a single seed entry for 0x756ED in `projects/scda/function_seeds.json` (full provenance text in the file). Once 0x756ED is disassembled as its own function, the existing `tail_jump_alias`/`tail_jump_target` pass logic automatically picks up 0x74873 too -- no second seed needed. Confirmed after the pipeline run: `sub_000756ED` (14 bytes, `seed_vtable_thunk`) and `sub_00074873` (22 bytes, `tail_jump_target`) are both now standalone entries in `functions.json` (total count 28144 -> 28146).

**Pipeline/build:** disasm -> func_id -> recomp -> `cmake --build` re-run in full, build log explicitly checked for 0 errors (no trusting a piped exit code). New build 2026-09-15 08:26:30, SHA-256 `d7d9105919a586329d568e557b233947dbd1f924dc9225cf8fda58945390dfce`.

**Functional verification:** a fresh boot run shows the old symptoms (`sub_00076402`, `sub_0024493D`, any reference to target 0x000756ED) completely gone. The boot visibly progresses further -- including a successful `[SCDA-UMD-READ]` of the default player profile (`[DefaultPlayer] Name=Player Class=EchelonCharacter.ESam ...`), which was not reached before. The process then crashes at a new location (minidump `SCDA_crash_2026-09-15_08-27-43.dmp`), triggered immediately after a `[ICALL] target 0x00000000 is not code ... source=0x00049F89` and a `[ABI] sub_0026940F: esi edi` violation.

**Still open:** the new blocker (`source=0x00049F89`, null target) and its associated `sub_0026940F` ABI violation are NOT investigated -- that is the task for the next round, using the same methodology. The other open items documented in Update 143 (`sub_001FA1BB`, `sub_00246CB4`, `0x080A080A`, the `0xC0000034` file-open failures) also remain unobserved in this run, either because they no longer occur or because they lie past the new, later crash point and were masked by it.

**Verified:** `git status` shows only `projects/scda/function_seeds.json` plus documentation as changed/new tracked files for this round; build log explicitly checked for 0 errors; the `functions.json` entries for 0x756ED/0x74873 verified against the Capstone reference; the scda_recomp process had already crashed on its own by the end of this round (minidump written), no manual termination needed.

## Update 145 (2026-09-15): New Blocker Characterized (Vtable Corruption on a Freshly-Constructed Object) -- NOT YET FIXED

**Starting point:** Update 144 fixed the `0x756ED`/`0x74873` blocker. New first blocker in a fresh boot log: `[ICALL] target 0x00000000 is not code ... source=0x00049F89`, followed by `[ABI] sub_0026940F: esi edi` and a crash.

**Live verification (cdb, several rounds):** at the `recomp_icall_not_code_log` breakpoint, `g_ecx=0`, `g_eax=0`, `MEM32(0x5ED158)=0x00000143` -- an obviously invalid heap-pointer value. `0x5ED158` is a global singleton pointer constructed in `sub_0004934E` (`recomp_0002.c:18600`, `MEM32(0x5ED158) = eax;`) and read back in the same function (line 18749, `ecx = MEM32(0x5ED158);`) immediately before calling `sub_001D8842` -- both sit in the same branch-free code path, so construction always precedes the read (proven both statically and live across several calls).

**First watchpoint run was misleading:** a plain data watchpoint on `0x5ED158` (armed for the whole process lifetime from launch) showed its FIRST hit as a self-write INSIDE `sub_001D8842` (`MEM32(0x5ED158) = ebx;`, `ebx=ecx=this`), initially looking like a missed/skipped construction (a suspected thread race). A combined run with a line breakpoint on the construction line AND the data watchpoint armed together disproved this: the construction line (18600) demonstrably fires FIRST, on the same call stack (`sub_000524DA -> sub_00054701 -> sub_00054722 -> sub_00048B15 -> sub_00048F1D -> sub_0004934E`, a worker thread spawned via `PsCreateSystemThreadEx`), with a perfectly valid `eax=0x012871D8`. The original watchpoint finding was a tooling artifact (cdb apparently swallowed the very first plain-watchpoint hit in that run) -- **no thread race**, no skipped construction.

**xemu ground truth (live, GDB remote protocol):** at the original VAs `0x49F11` (write) and `0x49FF3` (read), real hardware showed the exact same sequence: a valid pointer written (`0xB06DD0`), then the same valid value read back immediately after. No sign of cross-thread divergence here -- both platforms construct and read the singleton correctly and in the same order.

**The real bug sits deeper:** inside `sub_001D8842` (called with `this=0x012871D8`, the just-correctly-constructed object), a later vtable dispatch (`eax = MEM32(ebx); ... call [eax+0xE0]`, original VA `0x1D93AC`) crashes: `MEM32(0x012871D8)` (the object's vtable field, offset 0) reads as `0x7A1AA206` -- an address range impossible for this XBE's code. A dynamic watchpoint placed directly on this specific object's vtable field (`ba w4 @@c++(g_eax)`, armed right after construction) never fired before the crash -- the vtable field is never explicitly written at all, correctly or otherwise. It holds raw, uninitialized allocator memory from the start.

**Object provenance:** the `eax` at construction comes from `sub_001FA486` (called at VA `0x49EFF`), a thin wrapper that only builds arguments and tail-delegates into `sub_000638CD` -- the SAME `sub_000638CD` already identified across Updates 128-141 as the config-cache/object-dispatch singleton with several swallowed-vtable-thunk siblings (the family from Update 115/141, `sub_002E7A6D`/`93`/`A1` among others). This strongly suggests yet another, previously-undiscovered instance of the same bug family: `sub_000638CD`'s internal dispatch, for this specific argument context (called from the PsCreateSystemThreadEx worker thread, with `ecx` sourced from `MEM32(0x5E6DF8)`), likely selects a construction thunk that -- as three times already this session (Updates 115, 141, 144) -- was never recognized as its own function by the disassembler due to a function-boundary-swallowing bug, so it never runs, leaving the object allocated but never given a vtable pointer.

**Still open (deliberate stopping point for this round):** the exact dispatch logic inside `sub_000638CD` for this argument context has not yet been traced byte-for-byte (a different branch than the `[esi+0xB0]` dispatch from Update 141). Next step: fully Capstone-disassemble `sub_000638CD`, identify the branch selected for `ecx=MEM32(0x5E6DF8)`, check its jump target against `functions.json` for another swallowing case (a `data_imm` xref, the same mov-ecx/test/je/jmp/ret signature as the three siblings already found), then run the same seed-fix cycle (disasm -> func_id -> recomp -> build -> verify) as in Updates 141/144. No patch was implemented since the exact root cause (which thunk is missing) is not yet proven byte-exact -- only the chain down to the vtable field itself was proven live.
