## Update 262: the 60fps mod located byte-exact; a real-time boot test
## finds a new, later blocker -- recomp reaches SCDA's clean loading
## screen, then the loading bar freezes solid

**1. 60fps mod located byte-exact.** The user provided two paths: the
original XBE (`Z:\...\tester Double Agent XBOX1\scda\default.xbe`) and
the patched one (`Z:\...\Tools\extract-xiso\scda\default.xbe`, which is
the actual source of this project's `game_files/scda/default.xbe`).
`cmp -l` shows **exactly ONE differing byte** between the two 6,307,840-byte
files, at file offset 2,962,311. Mapped through the XBE section table to
guest VA **0x002E3387** (inside `.text`). Capstone disassembly shows the
exact instruction:
```
0x002e3385: mov dword ptr [eax], 0x80000002   ; original (30 FPS)
0x002e3385: mov dword ptr [eax], 0x80000001   ; patched (60 FPS)
```
The instruction sits inside a small setter function (VA
~0x002E3375-0x002E33B4) that, depending on an argument (1/2/default),
sets a field at `[ecx+0x4DD0]` to 1, 2, or this sentinel value.
`0x80000002`/`0x80000001` are the classic Xbox D3D presentation-interval
values `D3DPRESENT_INTERVAL_TWO` (sync every 2nd vblank, 30Hz) vs.
`D3DPRESENT_INTERVAL_ONE` (every vblank, 60Hz) -- the standard technique
for unlocking frame rate. **Since this project already uses the patched
XBE as its source, the patch is automatically present in every current
build; no action needed.** Explains, as the user predicted, the faster
intro timing compared to unmodified hardware.

**2. Direct real-time boot test** (user question: "do we reach the menu
with 'Press Start' after ~30s?"): launched `scda_recomp.exe` normally (no
debugger, full real-time speed) with `RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1` +
`RECOMP_FB_DUMP`, collecting screenshots roughly every 10s over several
minutes. Result:
- **At ~30s:** still on the Ubisoft logo (identical to the already-known
  Update 259 screenshot, same noise artifacts).
- **At ~40s:** already WAY past that -- the full **SCDA title screen**
  ("Tom Clancy's SPLINTER CELL DOUBLE AGENT", character portrait,
  crosshair overlay, "LOADING..." bar) appears, **completely cleanly,
  with no noise whatsoever.**
- **From roughly 3 minutes to at least 5 minutes:** the loading bar is
  **frozen solid** -- an exact pixel comparison (count of bright pixels
  in the bar's row) between the frame at ~3 min and the frame at ~5 min
  gives identically 198 bright pixels, zero pixels of progress. The
  process itself keeps running (still producing a new GPU report/
  screenshot every ~10s, so not fully frozen), but the visible loading
  makes no further progress. "Press Start" is NOT reached within the
  observed 5 minutes.

**Proven:** (a) the 60fps patch is fully identified and already active
automatically. (b) recomp now reliably and CLEANLY (no artifacts) reaches
the SCDA title/loading screen -- further real progress beyond the bare
Ubisoft logo. (c) immediately after that, a NEW, not-yet-investigated
blocker follows: the loading process visibly hangs even though the
process itself keeps running.

**Open / exact next test:** once the Ubisoft-logo noise artifacts
(Updates 260-261c) are resolved, or in parallel: investigate the loading-
screen freeze. First step per project convention: with
`RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1`, check whether `s_gpu.draws`/`unhandled_total` still
increase between two "frozen" reports (does only the display hang, or
does the game logic/loading itself hang too?), and compare a thread dump
(CDB `~*kb`) at two points during the freeze to locate the stuck code
path -- exactly the established methodology from earlier steady-state
investigations (e.g. after Update 232/233).

**Relevant artifacts:** `tools/debug/fbdump_update262_menucheck/` (31
screenshots over ~5 minutes of real-time boot; `frame003.png`/
`frame018.png`/`frame030.png` show the title screen at increasing times
with the loading bar frozen). No code changed. Process stopped cleanly

User observation while watching the debug window live ("nothing is
moving anymore"). Exact pixel comparison of the loading bar across all

(~60s) IMMEDIATELY at 198 bright pixels and stays at exactly 198 through
frame022 (at least ~220s runtime) -- zero pixels of progress since the

```
sub_00052CDC (KeDelayExecutionThread, kernel ordinal 99 -- translation
already confirmed byte-exact correct in Update 169)
  <- sub_00054701/sub_00054722 <- sub_00048B15 <- sub_0004934E
  <- sub_001CB75C <- sub_00038C3F <- sub_00072989 <- sub_00052D5A
  <- bridge_PsCreateSystemThreadEx <- xbe_entry_point <- main
```
`sub_00052CDC`'s own code (`recomp_0002.c:51625-51707`) shows a classic
polling retry: an indirect call through `MEM32(0x4F52F4)`,
`if (Handle != 0 && ReturnValue == 0x101) goto retry;` -- the called
kernel wait function keeps returning the same "not done yet" code, the
expected signal never arrives.

222 (2026-09-21) documented a structurally similar stall
(`sub_004A12B0`, polling a PFIFO/PGRAPH bit) with a clear cause: the NV2A
device pointer `MEM32(0x4AB668)` held `0x7400087D` -- far outside the
64MB guest RAM, i.e. not a real device. **Checked live in this run:
`MEM32(0x4AB668) = 0x004AB670`, a plausible, valid value within guest
RAM.** That old gap does not apply here -- thread 3 (a worker thread) was
briefly seen inside that same `sub_004A12B0` area at one point, but had
already left it (no longer spinning there) by the second snapshot. The
current stall is a NEW instance of the same general pattern ("main
thread waits for a signal some other thread/kernel function never
sets"), at a different, not-yet-documented location -- and sits much
LATER in the boot sequence than the entire Update 168-222 investigation
chain (which was exclusively about the period BEFORE any rendering
happened). This is therefore genuine new progress, not a regression.

**Proven:** (a) the cache directory identified, backed up, cleared,
nothing lost. (b) a real, reproducible red-flicker artifact exists at the
scene transition, structurally matching the user's hypothesis, though its
connection to cache state is not yet proven. (c) the loading-screen stall

## Update 265: the loading-screen stall's exact retry/wait condition fully
## reconstructed -- the main thread waits for a spawned worker thread's
## TERMINATION, and that worker's start routine looks like an intentionally
## endless tick loop (suspected semantic mismatch, not yet proven against
## xemu)

Per the user's instruction: stop analyzing the delay function itself
(`sub_00052CDC`/`KeDelayExecutionThread`) -- it is only the waiting side --
and instead determine the caller, the checked status value, the checked
handle/object, the condition that should end the loop, and the expected
producer thread. Minimal-invasive one-shot instrumentation, no permanent
polling.

**1. The actual poll loop lives in `sub_00038C3F`, not the delay function.**
`sub_00052CDC` is only reached through the sleep helper `sub_00072989`; the
function that decides WHETHER to wait again is `sub_00038C3F`
(`recomp_0001.c:35834ff`):

```
edi = 0x103;                          // STILL_ACTIVE-like sentinel
status = edi;
retry:
  sub_000523F7(handle=MEM32(esi+0xF4), &status);   // query status
  sub_00072989(MEM32(0x5A6F0C));                    // sleep
  if (status == 0x103) goto retry;                  // wait again
```

**2. `sub_000523F7` is structurally `ObReferenceObjectByHandle` + a status
check + `ObfDereferenceObject`** (`recomp_0002.c:49373ff`, the exact
pattern from Updates 170/233): the handle is resolved through IAT slot
`0x4F51A0` (fastcall object reference, 3rd param = an output pointer that
overwrites the handle slot itself with the resolved object pointer); then:
```
if (MEM8(object+4) == 0)        status = 0x103;   // "not done yet"
else                             status = MEM32(object+0x120);
```
These offsets are exactly `KTHREAD_DONE_OFFSET=4` /
`KTHREAD_EXITCODE_OFFSET=0x120` from `kernel_bridge.c:350-352` -- the
awaited object is provably the fake KTHREAD structure of a worker thread
spawned via `PsCreateSystemThreadEx`, whose "done" byte is set only by
`bridge_mark_thread_done()`, which in turn only fires when the worker's own
routine returns (normally or via `PsTerminateSystemThread`).

**3. Live proof (non-invasive `cdb` attach against a fresh run of
`build/scda_upgrade/bin/RelWithDebInfo/scda_recomp.exe`, breakpoint on
`sub_000523F7`'s entry instead of unreliable source-line breakpoints -- see
the methodology note below):**
- Handle argument on the caller's stack: `0x48000007` (bridge handle tag
  `0x48000000`, index 7).
- `s_handle_kthread_va[7] = 0x013fb000`.
- At that address: `DONE byte(+4) = 0x00`, `EXITCODE(+0x120) = 0x00000000`
  -- the worker is provably not done yet.
- **The process has exactly 3 threads at this point** (via `~*kb`): thread
  0 (main, in the retry loop described above), thread 1
  (`nv2a_ack_thread`, the runtime's own GPU-busy-bit acknowledger), thread 2
  (a real worker spawned via `CreateThread` through
  `bridge_thread_main`/`bridge_run_thread_inline`).
- **Thread 2's own TLS value `g_thread_kthread_va = 0x013fb000` -- an exact
  match.** This proves beyond doubt that thread 0 is waiting specifically
  for thread 2's termination; no stale-handle/misassignment hypothesis is
  needed to explain the correlation.

**4. Thread 2 itself is NOT stuck in the historical Update 222 trap -- it
merely passes through the same code periodically.** At the moment of
capture thread 2's PC was inside `sub_004A12B0` (the PFIFO/PGRAPH
"kick-bit" function from Update 222); a targeted memory check of the full
pointer chain shows: `MEM32(0x4AB668)=0x004ab670` (valid) ->
`MEM32(+0x1C28)=0xFD000000` (exactly the real NV2A aperture base) -> the
kick bit at `+0x100410` is **currently 0 (clear), not stuck set.** Two
snapshots a few seconds apart caught thread 2 at two DIFFERENT, advancing
instruction addresses inside that function (not the same spin instruction)
-- thread 2 is not blocked there, it simply revisits this function
repeatedly as part of its own periodic loop (`sub_000524DA` ->
`sub_00036889` -> `sub_00039566`, a sleep-paced loop that calls vtable
methods `+0x118`/`+0x11C` of an object at `MEM32(0x5E3E2C)` and would only
terminate if the global abort flag `MEM32(0x5ED140)` becomes nonzero).

**Tentative assessment (not yet conclusively proven):** `sub_00039566`
structurally resembles a persistent tick/render loop (accumulates a frame
delta, calls vtable methods on a session object, sleeps ~100 units per
iteration) rather than a one-shot loading job. If that assessment holds,
this worker can never return under normal circumstances, making
`sub_00038C3F`'s wait for its termination a semantic mismatch -- either real
hardware waits on a DIFFERENT signal here (not thread exit), or the wrong
worker slot/handle is being awaited at this call site. Not yet verified
against xemu.

**Methodology note (important for future sessions):** in this x64-native
RelWithDebInfo build, every emulated x86 register (`eax`, `esi`, `ebp`,
etc.) is a `RECOMP_TLS` global prefixed `g_` (e.g. `g_esp`, `g_esi`,
`#define esi g_esi` in `templates/runtime/recomp_types.h:1046-1051`) --
**these are `uint32_t`, but `poi()` reads 8 bytes on x64 and silently reads
into the next TLS variable.** Always use `dwo()` for these registers; only
use `poi()` for genuine 64-bit pointers like `g_xbox_mem_offset`. Also:
source-line breakpoints (`` bp `file.c:NNNN` ``) can land on reordered/
wrong code in this optimized build (observed: landing inside an ICALL
dispatch-table lookup instead of the expected simple assignment) --
function-name breakpoints (`bp module!function`) proved reliable and were
used for the decisive capture.

**Proven:** (a) the exact retry condition (status value, call chain,
handle, target structure) of the loading-screen stall. (b) thread 0
provably waits for thread 2's termination specifically -- no other
interpretation needed. (c) thread 2 is not blocked in the Update 222 PFIFO
trap at the moment of capture; the pointer chain and kick bit are fine.

**Refuted:** that the current stall is identical to the old Update 222
root cause (the device pointer is valid, the kick bit is clear).

## Update 271: reliably caught sub_000491BA's write path via a hardware
## watchpoint -- Case A confirmed: both input fields are already 0, the
## arithmetic/store themselves are correct

**Important methodology pitfall (hit first, then corrected):** a first
attempt to catch the write path via `gu` (return from `sub_000443D0`) plus
manual single-stepping (`p`) appeared to show `[ecx+0x48]=0x005e6e20`
(suspicious -- looked like an address rather than a tick value) --
**this was a measurement error.** The single-stepped disassembly after `gu`
showed completely different instructions than expected (comparisons
against constants like `0x39C`/`0x394`/`0x398`, not simple field accesses)
-- the optimizer reordered code around the call site, so the native
instruction sequence does NOT match source-line order. Instruction
counting after `gu` is **not reliable** in this optimized build. See
`tools/debug/update271_write_capture_out.log` for the discarded attempt.

**Robust method (works regardless of code reordering):** set a hardware
watchpoint (`ba w4 <hostaddr>`) directly on `0x5E6E04` as soon as
`sub_000491BA` is entered (host address computed live from
`g_xbox_mem_offset + 0x5E6E04`). This catches the REAL store regardless of
which source line CDB attributes it to (here: it misattributed it to
`recomp_0002.c:16202` instead of the expected line 16201 -- a debug-info
imprecision from optimization; the watchpoint itself is exact). Script:
`tools/debug/cdb_update271_watchpoint.txt`.

**Result (`tools/debug/update271_watchpoint_out2.log`):**
```
g_ecx=0x011051c8  g_eax=0x010f9e58  g_edx=0x00000000
[ecx+0x48]=0x00000000   [eax+0x48]=0x00000000
new_0x5E6E04 (after store) = 0x00000000
```
**Both input fields are already 0.** The summation (`edx=0+0=0`) and the
store itself are provably CORRECT -- no bug in `sub_000491BA`'s arithmetic,
no address/aliasing issue at the store (Case C ruled out), no skipped
branch before the write site (Case D ruled out, the store is provably
reached and executed). **This is unambiguously Case A.**

`ecx`/`eax` (`0x011051c8`/`0x010f9e58`) look like genuine heap object
pointers (not the stack address suspected earlier -- that was part of the
measurement error above). Both are obtained shortly before via
`sub_00067886` (`recomp_0002.c:16167`, delivers the `ecx` object
indirectly via `ebp-18188`) and the return value of `sub_000443D0`
(`recomp_0002.c:16194`, delivers the `eax` object). The `+0x48` field on
both objects looks like "duration/tick length of this animation or audio
segment" (context: `sub_000491BA` sums several consecutive field offsets,
`+0x48/+0x4C/+0x50/+0x54/+0x58`, each into a global `0x5E6Exx`/`0x5E76xx`
value -- looks like a crossfade/blend-duration aggregation between two
segments, not yet conclusively identified).

**Proven:** the frozen `0x5E6E04` denominator is NOT caused by a bug inside
`sub_000491BA` itself (neither arithmetic/signedness/store nor a skipped
branch) -- the function does exactly the right thing with the inputs it
receives. The inputs themselves (`[ecx+0x48]`, `[eax+0x48]`) are both 0.

**Refuted:** any hypothesis that looks for the cause inside
`sub_000491BA`'s own code (Cases B/C/D) -- all ruled out by the watchpoint

## Update 272: found the constructor and the generic virtual Read() call
## that should have populated +0x48 (and four sibling fields) -- the trail
## now leads to a stream/resource object whose content is not yet
## identified

**Object identification (via the watchpoint snapshot, `db` dump of both
objects):** both objects (`ecx=0x011051c8`, `eax=0x010f9e58`) are
**byte-for-byte identical except for one pointer field at +0x3C** -- two
freshly constructed instances of the same class, sharing vtable
`0x004F6F08`. `+4` holds the same value `0x64` (100) on both -- a
type/class constant, not per-instance data. This matches the `id=0x64/0x65`
seen in Update 270's list dump -- these are the same two objects.

**Constructor found:** `sub_000442B0` (`recomp_0001.c:84452`) sets up the
vtable, sets `+0x3C = ecx` (the constructor's own parameter, presumably a
stream/config object pointer), then calls **`sub_00036582(source=
MEM32(esi+0x3C), dest=&(esi+offset))` five times in a row** for `+0x48`,
`+0x4C`, `+0x50`, `+0x54`, `+0x58`. This is exactly the site that should
have populated `+0x48`.

**`sub_00036582` is a generic virtual "Read" wrapper**
(`recomp_0001.c:26921`): `esi=source; eax=MEM32(esi) [source's vtable];
call MEM32(eax+4)(this=source, dest, size=4);` -- reads 4 bytes through a
virtual method of the SOURCE (not the target object!) into the target
field. A classic "deserialize along a stream/resource" pattern. If the
source (the stream/config object at `+0x3C`, itself handed into the
constructor via `MEM32(ebp+8)`) is empty, at EOF, or was never properly
opened, `Read()` returns no real data -- the target fields stay at their
preset value `0`, exactly as observed.

**Proven:** the full chain from the frozen `0x5E6E04` denominator (Update
270), through `sub_000491BA`'s correct-but-starved store (Update 271, Case
A), down to the constructor and the generic `Read()` call that should have
populated `+0x48`, is now unbroken and backed by live memory dumps, not
just code reading.

**Refuted:** nothing new this step -- this is a direct deepening/
confirmation of the Case A lead from Update 271.

compared across separate launches.

**Conditional breakpoint actions with nested `.if{...}`/`.printf` DO work
reliably in this sandbox** (reproduced repeatedly, clean output) as long as

address `0x442E4` for the first `+0x48` read):**

## Update 274 (MAXIMUM tier): Hypothesis A confirmed, more precisely than
## expected -- the existing Update 220/221 cursor fix produces an
## out-of-window position on a full, non-EOF transfer, feeding the decoder
## garbage. `ebx+0x58` is definitively the real consumer/decoded-output
## address (Hypothesis B refuted).

**Full field map of the ring-buffer object (`ebx`, here `0x01135928`),
reconstructed from actual code usage in `sub_00040821`
(`recomp_manual.c:3584-3894`) -- no offset-proximity guessing, every row
backed by either live capture or direct code reading:**

| Offset | Meaning | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `+0x3C` | Handle to the open file (real Win32 HANDLE via bridge token) | Update 273, `s_handle_table` correlation |
| `+0x44` | Remaining/total file size (raw size field feeding the read request) | live: `0x001d5f71` = 1,924,977 -- exactly `common.lin`'s size (Update 221) |
| `+0x48` | Running total of requested bytes (caller-side progress counter) | `MEM32(ebx+0x48) += eax(=size)` at function entry |
| `+0x4058` | Physical buffer CAPACITY, constant, never written inside this function | live: `0x00024000` (= 0x4000 shadow/wrap zone + 0x20000 main window) |
| `+0x405C` | Fixed BASE POINTER of the physical fill buffer (a pointer, not instance data) | live: `0x01139998`, read constantly throughout the function, never written |
| `+0x4060` | Read/write CURSOR within the physical buffer (0..capacity) | live before first fill: `0x00024000` (== capacity, i.e. initial state is "empty/exhausted") |
| `+0x4064` | Accumulated total transferred bytes (pure statistics field) | `MEM32(ebx+0x4064) += eax(=transferred)` |
| `+0x4C` | Read cursor within the logical consumer buffer starting at `+0x58` | `MEM32(ebx+0x4C)=0` after each successful decode, then `+= eax` on consume |
| `+0x50` | Available bytes in the logical consumer buffer (`avail`) | drives the branch at `loc_00040847`; set to whatever `sub_000503EE` reports after decode |
| `+0x58` | **The consumer/decoded-output buffer itself** (inline destination address, not a pointer field) | passed directly as `arg1=ebx+0x58` to `sub_000503EE`; the consume code reads `ebx+0x58+cursor` directly as a memory address (no pointer dereference there) |

**Consumer address formula, derived from control flow and confirmed live
(refutes Hypothesis B):** consumer address = `ebx + 0x58 +
MEM32(ebx+0x4C)`. Not a pointer, not a vector control block -- a directly
embedded inline buffer. `ebx+0x58` is never written independently except
by the decode call itself; there is no separate "real" consumer address
elsewhere.

**Decisive new finding -- `sub_000503EE` is the decoder, not
`sub_00040821` itself:** after header parsing (`loc_000409A9`),
`sub_00040821` calls **`sub_000503EE(dest=ebx+0x58, &avail_out,
rawDataPtr, rawSize)`** (`recomp_manual.c:3845`, `recomp_0002.c:41668`).
`sub_000503EE` constructs a generic 56-byte "reader" object (vtable
`0x4F7B2C`) wrapping `(rawDataPtr, rawSize, dest, *avail_out_initial)`,
calls its virtual `Read()` method (`sub_0004E371`), and only treats return
value `1` as success (then `*avail_out = MEM32(ebp-36)`); any other return
value bails out WITHOUT writing `dest` or `*avail_out` at all.
**`sub_00040821` never checks `sub_000503EE`'s return value** and blindly
copies `*avail_out` into `ebx+0x50` regardless of success or failure.

**Live proof of the complete causal chain (single run,
`cdb_update274_capacity_check.txt` + `cdb_update274_decode_capture.txt`,
object `0x01135928`, the file in this particular run is really
`common.lin`, 1,924,977 bytes):**
1. Before the first fill: `capacity=0x24000`, `position=0x24000` (initial
   state = "fully exhausted"), `fillbase=0x1139998`,
   `sizefield(+0x44)=0x1d5f71`.
2. First internal read (`sub_000516B7`, return address `0x408E1`): target
   `fillbase+edx(0x4000)=0x113D998`, length `0x20000`, **transfers
   `0x20000` (full, no EOF)** -- confirms Update 273.
3. Cursor formula (the Update 220/221 fix, `loc_000408F0`): `new_position
   = transferred - MEM32(ebp-12)[=remaining_before=capacity-position=0]
   = 0x20000 - 0 = 0x20000`.
4. Header parsing (`loc_00040909`) reads at `fillbase+position =
   fillbase+0x20000 = 0x1159998` -- **0x1C000 bytes DEEP into the
   just-written 0x20000-byte block, not at its start** -- and gets real
   but meaningless bytes as the "header" (the second header dword is
   large enough to trigger a second fill).
5. A second internal read happens (return address `0x40983`), target
   again `0x113D998` (after compacting the remaining 0x3FF8 bytes to the
   buffer's front), again transfers the full `0x20000` -- confirms
   Update 273's second observation.
6. Cursor formula again: `0x20000 - 0x3FF8 = 0x1C008`.
7. `srcPtr` for the decode call = `fillbase+position =
   0x1139998+0x1C008 = 0x011559A0` -- **exactly the value measured live**
   in `sub_000503EE`'s parameters (the `decode_capture` log).
   `srcSize=0x301f96af` is the (meaningless) second "header" value from
   step 4.
8. `sub_0004E371` (the generic `Read()` method) returns `-3` (not
   success=1) -- `sub_000503EE` returns `-3` WITHOUT writing `*avail_out`
   or `dest`.
9. `sub_00040821` ignores this failure and blindly copies `*avail_out`
   (unchanged = stale stack garbage) into `ebx+0x50` -- matches the
   values repeatedly measured in Updates 271/273
   (`ring_avail=0x25e79286`, the `ebx+0x58` region staying completely
   zero because `dest` was never written).

**Proven:** the cursor/position formula from the existing Update 220/221
fix (`eax = transferred - MEM32(ebp+-12)`, at BOTH `loc_000408F0` and
`loc_00040992`) is structurally wrong for a FULL, non-EOF transfer (when
up to `0x20000` requested bytes actually all arrive): it places the header-
parsing position deep inside the payload block instead of at its start.
The original (pre-Update-220, then-recognized-as-buggy) formula used the
constant `0x4000` instead; whether the *correct* original semantics is
"position modulo/relative to the fixed 0x4000 mark" or something else has
NOT yet been checked against the real original x86 bytes -- that is the
next step, not a guess.

**Refuted:** Hypothesis B (`ebx+0x58` was misread as the consumer
address) -- the address is unambiguously correct, used directly as the
decoder's destination buffer. Also refuted: any hypothesis placing the
defect in disk I/O, the kernel bridge, the file size, or the consumer's
own copy code -- the defect is exclusively in the position formula that
feeds the decoder wrong source data, plus the missing error check
afterward.

**Active next test:** read the original x86 bytes of `sub_00040821`
exactly at `loc_000408F0` and `loc_00040992` (Capstone, addresses
`0x000408F0`/`0x00040992` onward, resolved through the XBE section
headers) byte-exactly: which register/stack slot does the ORIGINAL code
really use for the new position, and how does it behave when a transfer
exceeds the capacity (0x24000) or the 0x4000 window? Goal: decide whether
the correct formula includes a modulo/clamp against `0x4000` or `capacity`
that the Update 220/221 fix accidentally dropped when it replaced the
constant. Only propose a correction AFTER this original-code proof -- no
cursor change without it, no bootstrap copy between the regions, no
symptom patch that bypasses the missing error check.

**Relevant artifacts:** `tools/debug/cdb_update274_capacity_check.txt`

## Update 276c: important correction -- sub_0003FCA5 is the STANDARD Xbox
## "problem with the disc" fatal error dialog, not a generic loading-image
## fallback. This reframes the open question.

**Found by decoding the 5 language-template string constants
(`0x4F67C8`, `0x4F6740`, `0x4F6690`, `0x4F6600`, `0x4F6550` and their
paired sub-strings) directly from the XBE as UTF-16LE text:**
```
EN: "There's a problem with the disc you're u[sing]" / "It may be dirty or damaged."
IT: "Il disco in uso ha qualche problema." / "Potrebbe essere sporco o danneggiato."
ES: "Hay un problema con el disco que est[a] us[ando]" / "Puede estar sucio o da[n]ado."
FR: "Le disque utilise presente une anomalie." / "Il est peut-etre sale ou endommage."
DE: "Bei der benutzten CD ist ein Problem auf[getreten]" / "Moeglicherweise ist sie verschmutzt oder [beschaedigt]."
```
This is the well-known, standard Xbox "disc problem" dialog text.
**`sub_0003FCA5` is therefore the game/SDK's built-in handler for a
genuine, unrecoverable disc I/O error**, not a generic "loading image
missing, show a placeholder" fallback as first assumed in Update 276b.
The `Menu_loading*.tga`/`SplinterCell3Logo.tga` files are most likely
background art FOR THIS ERROR DIALOG itself, not for normal level
loading. An unconditional infinite idle after showing this message is
entirely reasonable for a "the disc is broken, nothing more can be done"
state and is very likely not a bug in itself.

**This reframes the actual open question.** It is no longer "why is a
generic loading image chosen instead of a level-specific one" but:
**"why does our run treat a simple, ordinary 'file not found' (opening
`SplinterCell3Logo.tga`/`Menu_loading*.tga`, which plainly do not exist)
as a catastrophic, unrecoverable disc error that triggers the standard
disc-error dialog?"** On real hardware, either (a) this path for a
missing, optional dialog background image never triggers the full
"disc is broken" handler at all -- the original call chain likely has an
early "did Open() fail? then don't even attempt to read, just proceed
without the background image" check that our recomp is missing or
evaluates incorrectly -- or (b) this whole code path is never reached on
real hardware for a simple missing optional file, because a caller
further up distinguishes "file not found" from "disc hardware error" and
only forwards the latter into `sub_00040821`'s error-callback mechanism.

**All three fields are exactly zero** -- this object never successfully

hypothesis in the previous status update) as the cause: `common.lin`'s
stream had provably already transferred real data (89969 bytes), while
our crashing object never transferred anything. The timing proximity was
pure coincidence (two independent streams active shortly after each
other in the same boot phase).

`0x01135928` is the same heap address observed in Updates 273-275 for the
very first, extensively traced generic reader object there (vtable
`0x004F6940`, a `sub_00040821` instance). Since heap addresses can be
reused within a run after being freed, this is most likely a NEW instance
of the same generic reader class (not necessarily the same logical
object), used for one of the failed candidates from the Update 276 chain

`Menu_loading.tga` -> all failed, unlike `SplinterCellLogo.tga` and
`Menu_loading.bik`, which both opened successfully) -- exactly consistent
with "Open() failed (file doesn't exist), size therefore never
determined, handle therefore 0, but `sub_00040821` reads anyway".

failure chain belongs to the `SplinterCell3Logo.tga`/`Menu_loading*.tga`
loading attempt series, NOT to `common.lin` or a side effect newly

## Update 279/280: counter values checked, but the follow-up experiment
## failed methodologically -- NO solid new result, only a methodology
## lesson.

**Update 279 (counters at `sub_0007F412`'s loop):** region/config flags
at execution time: `0x5ED104=0`, `0x5ED140=1`, `0x5ED144=0` (look like
plausible, small boolean config values, NOT like obviously corrupted/
uninitialized values such as `0xCCCCCCCC`). The three parallel counters at
this point: `[+0x40]=5649 [+0x48]=1552 [+0x50]=89`. **89 is far larger
than the 6 observed `Menu_loading` filename attempts** -- this refutes the
simple assumption "esi+0x50 IS the Menu_loading candidate list directly,
1:1". The actual candidate iteration (0/1/2/3/4/5/bare) therefore most
likely lives DEEPER (e.g. as generic "try N numbered variants" logic
inside the resource-open method itself, applied to exactly ONE of the 89
catalog entries), not in this enumeration loop itself.

**Update 280 (attempt to identify the exact catalog entry) --
METHODOLOGICALLY FAILED, result NOT usable:** a breakpoint on
`sub_0007DE25` filtered by return address (`0x7f7a2`) WITHOUT a hit-count
cap caught **468,393 hits** (log grew to 92 MB), with monotonically
increasing, never-repeating addresses (0x20-byte steps) and all-zero
content throughout. This does NOT match "re-iterating 89 entries of a
fixed list" -- either `0x7f7a2` is not as unique a return address as
assumed (e.g. a completely different, frequently-called call site happens
to share the same low-value address), or a very large, mostly-empty
memory region is genuinely being scanned continuously (e.g. as part of
normal, ongoing game engine work unrelated to the boot blocker).
**Deliberately no conclusion is drawn from this experiment.** The process
was manually terminated; the 92 MB log file
(`update280_iteminfo_out.log`) is left untouched (no diagnostic artifacts
deleted, per standing rule), but must NOT be treated as solid evidence in
a future session.

**Methodology lesson for the next session:** every unconditional
breakpoint with an action MUST either (a) disable itself after the first
hit (`bc N`), or (b) carry a counter with a fixed cap
(`.if (@$tX >= LIMIT) { bc N } .else { g }`) BEFORE it is started --
otherwise a frequently-invoked code path can generate unbounded hits,
wasting both time and disk space without yielding usable new information.

**Active next test (substance unchanged, refined):** do not search for the

## Update 285: RESOLVED -- the sixfold repetition is NOT inside
## sub_00039566's call graph; it is a SELF-CONTAINED retry loop inside a

Full read of `sub_00037D14` (`recomp_0001.c:32577-32826`) shows the

- `test eax,eax; jne` -- on success (eax != 0) jumps straight to the
  shared endpoint `loc_00037E0B`.
- On failure (eax == 0, `loc_00037DE5`) calls `sub_000677A4(&tried[6],
  &lastIndex, 6)` to check whether untested slots remain: `test eax,eax;
  jne loc_00037D5D` -- if yes, jumps BACK to the draw point (next random
  index, duplicates skipped); if NO (all 6 slots tested and failed),
  falls through to `loc_00037DFF` and lands at the SAME `loc_00037E0B`
  endpoint as the success case.

exactly explains Update 283's permutation finding (6 hits, values
5,3,4,0,2,1, all within ONE call), and is PROVABLY faithful original

## Update 289: root-cause mechanism of the handle corruption found and
## Capstone-verified -- the wrap-around memcpy itself is a byte-exact,
## faithful translation of the original (NOT a new recompiler bug); the
## real trigger is a non-4-byte-aligned cursor value that can only be
## explained by an integer underflow in the SAME position formula already
## touched in Updates 220/221/274/275, inherited from an EARLIER call to
## `sub_00040821` on this same object.

**Live capture 5 result** (`tools/debug/cdb_update289_corruption.txt` /
`update289_corruption_out.log`, after fixing an invalid pseudo-register
name `$ta`/`$tb` -> only `$t0`-`$t19` are valid, corrected to `$t11`/
`$t12`):

    WRITE #2-#5  ebx=0x01135928 edi=0x0111d999 esi=0x0113d999 ecx=0x00007fff
                 edx=0x00004000 bufptr(+405C)=0x01139998 bufsize(+4058)=0x00024000
                 cursor(+4060)=0x00004001 declsize(+44)=0x001d5f71

`edi=0x0111d999` sits ~113 KB BEFORE the buffer start (`bufptr=0x01139998`),
and the `rep movsd`/memcpy writes `ecx*4=0x1FFFC` (~128 KB) bytes from
there -- a range that runs straight over our object (`0x01135928`) and its
handle field (`+0x3C`).

**Capstone verification** (`tools/debug/capstone_update289.py`, original
XBE `0x00040909-0x000409AF`) shows an instruction-for-instruction IDENTICAL
sequence to the generated C (`mov eax,[ebx+4060]` / `mov edi,[ebx+405c]` /
... / `lea esi,[eax+edi]` / `sub edi,ecx` / `add edi,edx` / `rep movsd` /
...). The wrap-around copy logic itself (`loc_00040942`,
`recomp_manual.c:3772-3786`) is therefore NOT a new recompiler bug -- it is
a faithful translation of the original game code.

**The actual trigger:** `cursor(+4060)=0x00004001` is NOT 4-byte-aligned,
even though this field is only ever advanced in units of 4 throughout this
function (`add eax,4` twice per header field read). `0x4001` falls out
exactly from the ALREADY-RESTORED original formula `eax = 0x4000 -
MEM32(ebp-12)` (Updates 220/221/274/275) if `MEM32(ebp-12)` ("remaining
buffer space after the OS transfer") was `0xFFFFFFFF` (or any value that
underflows the subtraction) during an EARLIER call to `sub_00040821` on
this same ring-buffer object: `0x4000 - 0xFFFFFFFF mod 2^32 = 0x4001`.
This means the invocation caught by the watchpoint is not itself at fault
-- it inherits an already-corrupted cursor from a PRIOR call (most likely
the object's first-ever wrap), reads a bogus "needed size" header field
from the wrong buffer position as a result, and that triggers this
wrap-around path with an underflowed destination address.

**Open question / next test:** whether `MEM32(ebp-12) > 0x4000` (i.e. the
OS-level read call returning MORE than 0x4000 bytes in a single
transfer) can happen on real hardware/xemu at all (e.g. because Xbox DVD
reads are granular differently there), or whether our own bridge
implementation of `NtReadFile`/`sub_000516B7` satisfies the host
filesystem call too generously in one shot instead of reproducing the
original's expected (smaller) transfer granularity -- which would make
this a genuine emulation-fidelity bug in the bridge, not a translation
error in the generated code. Next step: instrument the formula site itself
(`recomp_manual.c`, `loc_000408F0`/`loc_00040992`, around lines 3722/3826)
live to log `MEM32(ebp-12)` on every call, confirm whether/when it ever
exceeds `0x4000`, and correlate that with the actual byte count
`sub_000516B7`/`xbox_NtReadFile` returns in a single transfer. No code fix
without this direct evidence (project rule: no symptomatic patches).

This is a completely PLAUSIBLE, monotonically increasing sequence, never

**Conclusion:** since every cdb run is a fresh process launch, and this
object's heap address is surprisingly stable across separate runs (always

whether this object performs a bad wrap itself or instead becomes the
VICTIM of some OTHER ring-buffer object's out-of-bounds wrap write) varies
between individual process launches -- a classic signature of genuine,
timing-/heap-layout-dependent memory corruption, not a single deterministic
line-level bug. The Capstone-verified wrap-copy instruction sequence from

plausible that SOME ring-buffer object in the system (not necessarily
always `0x01135928` itself) executes this wrap with an underflowed cursor
and overwrites neighboring heap memory (sometimes `0x01135928`'s own handle

## Update 293: Update 292's cross-object bufsize check was a NO HIT
## despite the fatal error recurring -- wrong invariant identified and
## corrected (methodology change, not a repeated identical run); also a
## new CDB scripting limitation discovered (`.if` does not support `||`).

**Update 292 result:** `FATAL-READ-ERROR ntstatus=0xc0000001
ring_obj=0x01135928 total_bad_transitions=0` -- none of the four cursor
formula write sites ever produced a value `> bufsize`, across ALL objects
in the system, before the known fatal error recurred. This means "new
cursor > buffer size" was the WRONG invariant for this corruption class:
Update 289's actually-observed corrupted value was `0x4001` -- small, well
within the valid range, but NOT 4-byte-aligned, even though this field is
only ever supposed to advance in multiples of 4. That misalignment is the
real warning sign, not exceeding the buffer size.

**Methodology change (not a third identical run, a corrected check):**
switched the condition to `(new_value & 3) != 0` (not 4-aligned) instead
of `new_value > bufsize`. A first attempt combining both conditions
(`(new_value > bufsize) || (not aligned)`) failed with a CDB syntax error
("Numeric expression missing") -- **new methodology finding: CDB's `.if`
expression evaluator does not support the `||` operator in this form.**
Reduced to the single, more targeted alignment check and restarted
(`update293_alignment_out.log`).

## Update 293 (continued): HIT -- the corrected alignment check found 4
## transitions, at least one of which is unambiguously a genuine
## miscalculation, on the exact target object.

**Result:**

    #1 writer=A(3751) obj=0x01135928 old=0x00024000 new=0x00000001 bufsize=0x00024000
    #2 writer=A(3751) obj=0x0115d9a8 old=0x00024000 new=0x00000001 bufsize=0x00024000
    #3 writer=D(3840) obj=0x01135928 old=0x000221de new=0x00015f71 bufsize=0x00024000
    #4 writer=A(3751) obj=0x01135928 old=0x00023ff9 new=0x00000001 bufsize=0x00024000
    FATAL-READ-ERROR ntstatus=0xc0000001 ring_obj=0x01135928 total_bad_transitions=4

**Assessment:** #1/#2/#4 (writer A, line 3751) all produce the same value
`1` right after a construction/near-buffer-end wrap state (`old` near/at
`bufsize`) -- arithmetically this means `MEM32(ebp-12)=0x3FFF` (a plausible,
small "remainder after transfer" of 16383 bytes). This is PROBABLY NOT
corruption, just a legitimately non-4-aligned case (file data doesn't have
to end on a 4-byte boundary) -- the alignment check by itself is too broad
and also flags harmless cases.

**#3 (writer D, line 3840) is unambiguously a genuine miscalculation:**
`new=0x15f71` from `old=0x221de` arithmetically requires `MEM32(ebp-12) =
0x4000 - 0x15f71 mod 2^32 = 0xFFFEE08F` (~4.29 billion) -- a value FAR
outside any plausible "remaining buffer" size, only explainable by an
integer underflow feeding into this formula (the incoming "remaining" must
already have been huge/negative). The stack trace confirms exactly the
call chain first found in Update 276
(`sub_0004438C -> sub_00045738 -> sub_0007DC43 -> sub_00036582 ->
sub_0007DE25 -> sub_0007F412 -> sub_00064B00`). The process kept running
normally for a while AFTER this hit (transition #4 shows a later, again
plausible buffer state) before the fatal error occurred -- so `0x15f71`
alone wasn't immediately fatal, it was a first confirmed malfunction in a
longer chain.

object goes GOOD->BAD, follow only its path"):** the wrap decision itself

## Update 299: FINAL MECHANISM FOUND -- the "2048-byte null-handle read"
## from Updates 297/298 is fully explained: it is our own common.lin
## object, already zeroed out entirely, after having correctly finished
## reading the whole file. Update 298's "unread device layer" hypothesis
## is refuted by a byte-exact Capstone read of sub_000516B7.

**Policy change applied first:** AGENTS.md's diagnostic timeout section
was rewritten to require a SYNCHRONOUS, technically enforced timeout
(e.g. the shell `timeout` command wrapping a foreground `cdb` invocation)
instead of scheduled wake-ups, which have proven unreliable in this
environment. All captures in this update ran this way (`timeout 570 cdb
...`, blocking in the same tool call, evaluated immediately on return).

**Capstone verification of `sub_000516B7`** (original XBE
`0x000516B7-0x0005179D`) confirms an exact match to the generated C, and
reveals: `MEM32(0x4F5240)` and `MEM32(0x4F5294)` are NOT function/vtable
pointers at all -- they hold the native Xbox kernel import encoding
`0x80000000 | ordinal`. `0x4F5240 = 0x800000DB` -> ordinal `0xDB` = 219 =
**NtReadFile directly**; `0x4F5294 = 0x800000E9` -> ordinal `0xE9` = 233
(the "pending" wait path). There is no hidden device/media abstraction
layer to read -- `sub_000516B7` calls the kernel directly with whatever
Length its own caller (`sub_00040821`) computed. Update 298's hypothesis
of an unread intermediate function is REFUTED.

**Live verification (one synchronous run, hard 10-minute timeout, per the
new policy):** measuring directly at the fatal-read-error breakpoint
itself (`sub_000516B7+0xaae`) shows:

    FATAL-READ-ERROR ... handle_field=0x00000000 declsize=0x00000000
        cursor=0x00000000 bufsize=0x00000000

ALL FOUR fields of the ring-buffer object are already zero at this exact
point. This fully explains the "2048-byte" mystery from Updates 297/298
without any extra assumption: `sub_00040821`'s size formula
(`eax=MEM32(ebx+0x44)>>0xB; eax++; eax<<=0xB`) with `declsize=0` computes
exactly `0>>11=0, +1=1, <<11=2048`. This is NOT a different, small object
-- it is **our own `common.lin` object (`0x01135928`)**, already fully
zeroed out after correctly finishing the entire 0x1d5f71-byte read
(Update 297). The separate, early `NULLHANDLE` event from Update
298/299 (object `0x00000000`, occurring right at boot, long before any
file open) is an INDEPENDENT, harmless, earlier occurrence and is NOT
causally linked to the actual fatal read error -- Update 298's "unified
theory" connecting the two was premature and is hereby corrected.

**FINAL OVERALL STATE of this exceptionally long investigation round
(Updates 265-299, 20+ live captures):** the original main blocker
(ring-buffer cursor formula, Updates 220/221/274/275) is fixed and
verified. The downstream, current blocker is now FULLY mechanistically
explained: `common.lin` (1,924,977 bytes) is read completely and
byte-exactly to the last byte (Update 297); afterward the object (handle,
declsize, cursor, bufsize) gets fully zeroed out (WHERE exactly this
happens is the one remaining open question, see below); DESPITE that, one
more refill attempt is made on this already-zeroed object, which -- due to
`declsize=0` -- arithmetically requests exactly 2048 bytes with a null
handle token, producing `STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL` (`0xc0000001`) and the boot
freeze.

**Open question / concrete next step (static first, then a SINGLE
targeted live check of one specific line, not a general capture):** WHO
zeroes `declsize` (`this+0x44`)? Known: neither `sub_000407F7` (Close,
only clears the handle field `+0x3C`, fully read in Update 288) nor the
destructor `sub_00040B00` (only conditionally calls Close and swaps the
vtable, no field reset) do this. Next step: grep for ALL writes to
`MEM32(ebx + 0x44)` across the generated sources (similar to the
four-site search for `+0x4060` in Updates 291/292), and look for any
`memset`-like pattern that could zero this object type as a whole (e.g. a
generic "reset/clear resource" method on a PARENT class that embeds this
ring-buffer object as a member). Only once a concrete write site is found,
check live and specifically (not "on suspicion") whether it fires BEFORE
or only as a result of the observed refill attempt, and Capstone-verify
the original x86 behavior there before considering any fix.

## Update 300: destructor hypothesis REFUTED (clean result, not a
## timeout); the all-zero-fields finding from Update 299 is reconciled
## with the Update 288/289 out-of-bounds wrap-copy mechanism as the most
## coherent explanation. FINAL STOPPING POINT for this investigation
## round.

**Policy change:** AGENTS.md's diagnostic timeout section was rewritten
to require a synchronous, technically enforced timeout (no scheduled
wake-ups) -- every diagnostic attempt must now return within the same
tool call via a mechanism like the shell `timeout` command wrapping a
foreground `cdb` invocation, evaluated immediately. All captures in this
update used `timeout 570 cdb ...` this way.

**Live test result:** instrumented `sub_00040B00` (the destructor, whose
own code -- fully read in Update 288 -- can free the ENTIRE object via
`sub_0029FA18(this)` when called with a delete flag set) filtered to
object `0x01135928`. Result: **`destructor_calls_on_target=0`** -- the
destructor was never called on this object before the fatal read error.
The full zeroing of all four fields observed in Update 299 is therefore
NOT caused by a regular destructor/delete operation.

**Reconciliation:** since neither `sub_000407F7` (Close, only touches the
handle field) nor the destructor (never called) explain the zeroing, and
since Update 288/289 already established a Capstone-verified, byte-exact-
to-original mechanism capable of producing exactly this kind of field
overwrite (the wrap-around `memcpy` in `loc_00040942`, whose destination
pointer can land far before the buffer and into the object's own header
when the cursor has underflowed), the most coherent explanation is:
**the full four-field zeroing in Update 299 is another manifestation of
the SAME out-of-bounds wrap-copy mechanism from Update 288/289** -- in
this particular run apparently with a different destination-pointer/
source-data combination that overwrites a wider range (all four header
fields instead of just the handle). This cleanly explains why the visible
symptom varies between runs (Update 291/294: no visible corruption;
Update 293: only the handle affected; Update 299: all four fields
affected) -- all are manifestations of the same data-content-dependent
wrap-copy miscalculation.

**FINAL OVERALL STATE (Updates 265-300, 20+ live captures):** the original
main blocker (cursor formula) is fixed and verified. The downstream
blocker is now mechanistically fully understood: a Capstone-verified,
faithful-to-original but data-content-dependent wrap-around copy operation
in `sub_00040821` (`loc_00040942`) can, when the cursor is corrupted by
upstream data (plausibly a host-vs-original disk-read transfer-granularity
mismatch), compute a destination pointer far outside the intended buffer
and overwrite part or all of the object's own header (handle, size,
cursor, buffer size) with arbitrary stream content (often zeros). A
subsequent refill attempt, misled by the now-corrupted (zero) values,
arithmetically requests exactly 2048 bytes with a null handle token,
producing `STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL` (`0xc0000001`) and the known boot freeze.
The EXACT code site/condition that FIRST corrupts the cursor (before the
wrap-copy processes it) could NOT be narrowed to a single deterministic
line despite 20+ targeted live captures -- the behavior is demonstrably
run-/timing-dependent.

**No code fix has been implemented in this entire round (Updates
276-300).** For a future session: either (a) specifically adjust
`xbox_NtReadFile`'s host transfer granularity to deliver smaller,
original-Xbox-like chunks (a bridge-fidelity change, requires knowing the
actual original transfer size, e.g. via an xemu comparison), or (b)
defensively guard the wrap-copy in `sub_00040821` against a detectably
implausible `remaining` value -- NEITHER should be implemented without
further direct confirmation (especially an xemu ground-truth comparison),
since either could otherwise amount to a symptomatic patch.

## Updates 343-344 (2026-09-26): xemu DSP56300 port; EP module table exposes a flag-lifting bug

### 343: port of the xemu GP/EP DSP

- Source: xemu `hw/xbox/mcpx/apu/dsp` at `f9b14039e5bb56ae2d8f028e31e7cc19f13f7e12`,
  C interpreter only, upstream files unmodified under `src/apu/dsp/`
  (provenance, licences GPL v2+/LGPL v2+ and the list of local adaptations:
  `src/apu/dsp/PROVENANCE.md`). QEMU is not pulled in: minimal shims in
  `src/apu/dsp/shim/` (`qemu/osdep.h`, `qemu/bswap.h`, `qemu/compiler.h`,
  `trace.h`, `ui/xemu-settings.h`) plus `dsp_jit_stub.c` (aborts if the
  JIT were ever selected; it never is).
- CMake: library `xbox_apu_dsp` (linked PUBLIC into `xbox_apu`) and the
  EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL test `apu_dsp_tests` (`tests/apu_dsp/test_apu_dsp.c`).
- `src/apu/apu_dsp.c` replaced by the adapted `gp_ep.c` (range cases ->
  `IN_RANGE`, GP/EP MMIO exported for `apu_core.c`, which now routes
  +0x30000 (GP) and +0x50000 (EP)). The old placeholder DSP state in
  `apu_state.h` became `#include "dsp.h"`. The old stub (and its
  `RECOMP_APU_DSP_ACK` doorbell ack) is gone -- no fake ready bits.
- Asserts: QEMU never builds with NDEBUG and the interpreter uses assert()
  as a runtime check. Compiled out, an out-of-range PC read host pointers
  from the opcode cache as instructions ("op = 00007ff6" segfault). The
  shim keeps asserts on.
- Memory model: DirectSound programs guest VAs as APU "physical" addresses
  (observed GPSADDR=0x84D4C000, SGE 0x84D40000/0x84D41000 -- our
  MmGetPhysicalAddress is the identity). The xemu-style 64 MB mask turned
  them into unrelated low pages (scratch word 0 read 0 instead of
  0x000BF080) and the GP booted an empty program (NOPs to P:0x800 ->
  assert). Fix: `apu_phys_ptr()/apu_phys_valid()` in `apu_shim.h` resolve
  guest addresses (base RAM + both contiguous regions 0x80000000-0x88000000)
  for all APU accessors, the VP ADPCM fetch and the DSP scatter-gather.
- Tests: `apu_dsp_tests` 19/19 (memory spaces incl. 0xCA fill, a
  three-instruction program, reset, separate GP/EP windows, GP bootstrap
  through an SGE table + one frame).
- Runtime with `RECOMP_AC97_READY=1 RECOMP_PB_EXEC=1 RECOMP_FB_WINDOW=1`:
  GP bootstraps the real program, the DirectSound wait at 0x4D1EF6 is gone,
  boot continues (new worker threads, file reads). New stop: the EP
  asserts on `extractu #CO,S2,D` (0x0C1890) at P:0x0519 -- an instruction
  xemu's interpreter (also current master) does not implement.

### 344: why the EP reaches extractu -- a lifter bug, not a DSP gap

- Diagnostics (opt-in, `RECOMP_DSP_TRACE=1`, `RECOMP_DSP_DISASM=1`):
  PC/disassembly ring (`src/apu/dsp/dsp_diag.c`, fed by the trace shim),
  dump of P/X memory and core registers on abort (SIGABRT handler), P
  memory after each GP bootstrap, EP scratch module table at EP bootstrap.
  Note: the interpreter's `core->is_gp` stays false for the GP; the
  running DSP is taken from apu_dsp.c's frame loop instead.
- EP boot code: module loader at P:0x180 (table at P:0x100, entry =
  (scratch offset, length)); X:$0BC3 selects the downmix module (1 ->
  module 5, 2 -> module 6). X:$0BC3 = 2 in recomp AND in xemu (stereo).
- EEPROM side fix: XC_AUDIO returned 0x00010001, commented "stereo + AC3"
  but meaning mono + AC3. Now `XC_AUDIO_FLAGS_STEREO` (0), matching xemu's
  generated EEPROM and the user's eee.bin (offset 0x98 = 0). Not the
  cause of the stop (same X:$0BC3 either way), but wrong before.
- Xemu ground truth (0.8.96, `tools/debug/xemu_update344_ep_state.py`,
  reads EP X/P memory through the APU MMIO window via the gdbstub; log
  `xemu344_ep_pmem.log` in the session scratchpad):
  no "Illegal instruction" in 150 s; P:0x010D (module 6 length) = 0xC9,
  recomp 0; offsets after it shifted by 0xC9 (0x1CFE vs 0x1C35). Recomp's
  EP therefore "loaded" module 6 with 0 words and called stale code at
  P:0x0304 that leads to the extractu. (P:0x011E/0x0120/0x0121 hold host
  pointers in both -- irrelevant differences.)
- Writer (cdb `ba w4` on the scratch word, `cdb_epmod_check.txt`):
  `sub_004D8FF7` builds the table from `sub_004D8E47(i, &ptr, &len)`, a
  switch whose case 5 is
  `dec eax ; mov eax,[ebp+0xc] ; je case5` -> (0x6C8658, 0xC9). The
  generated C tested `eax == 0` after the mov had replaced eax, so case 5
  fell into the default (len 0).
- Generic fix in `tools/recomp/lifter.py`: before an EFLAGS-preserving
  instruction writes a register/memory the tracked condition would re-read
  (all setters except cmp/test/bsf/bsr/cmpxchg, which already snapshot),
  the operand values are copied into function temps `_fsv0/1/2` (width
  suffix w/b keeps 8/16-bit conditions right) and the flag state reads
  those; `translator.py` declares them when used. x87/SSE compare setters
  are not covered (non-GPR operands) -- known limitation.
  Regression tests `tools/recomp/test_flag_operand_clobber.py` (7); whole
  recomp suite green.
- First version of the fix was too broad: 58231 copies, among them
  `_fsv0 = esp;` right after `sub esp, N` in prologues (11634) -- that line
  contains "esp" and ended `_fixup_icall_esp_save`'s prologue scan early,
  i.e. the Update 232 failure class again (wild icalls, ABI mismatches).
  Refined: copy only when a flag reader (jcc/setcc/cmovcc/adc/sbb/rcl/rcr/
  lahf/pushfd) follows before the flags are redefined (a call ends the
  search, a call never triggers a copy; falling off the block counts as a
  possible read), and the prologue scans skip `_fsv` lines. 5324 sites.
  Tests 9/9, suite green.
- Verified build 2026-09-26 16:44:06, SHA-256
  `eea6c90d6ffafbdf5b73e2963e0f1afe05319f24d1a90b58e8e87839d458065f`
  (31973/31976 functions, 0 failed). Runtime: EP runs module 6 (loop
  P:0x369-0x378), no extractu. File opens now match xemu exactly up to
  `logos.bik` (DynamicXbox.umd, Stream.SS2, Fol_Common.SS2, common.lin,
  splintercell4xboxretail.umd, Menu.lin, logos.bik); xemu continues with
  lipsyncxbox.umd, Menu.SS2, back_menu.bik.
- Next blocker: ~80 s in, during logos.bik, Bink `sub_004BB020` iterates
  `[edi+0x308]` (count `[edi+0x300]`) and calls `[entry+0x18]`: garbage
  targets from source 0x004BB094 (>10^8 icall failures), then an assert
  `addr % 4 == 0` on a GP register-window write (unaligned APU access,

### 344b: rdtsc, a shadowed runtime header, first Bink frame

- Why the Bink track loop ran at all: xemu never reaches `sub_004BB020` in
  170 s (`tools/debug/xemu_update344_bink_tracks.py`). Two triggers exist:
  `sub_004BB1B0` via `[bink+0x2F4]`, set only by `sub_004B8CD0` when
  RADTimerRead advanced > 300000 ms since the last sync, and
  `sub_004BB790` via a per-track underrun flag `[track+0x5C]`.
- RADTimerRead (`sub_004BC570`) uses QPF = `sub_00371B30` (constant
  0x2BB5C755 = 733333333) and QPC = `sub_00371B1F` = bare `rdtsc`, which
  the lifter emitted as `/* TODO: rdtsc */` -- edx:eax stale. Fix: lifter
  emits `recomp_rdtsc()`; runtime (`xbox_memory_layout.c`) returns a
  monotonic 733.333333 MHz count derived from the host QPC. Test
  `tools/recomp/test_lifter_rdtsc.py`; 236 rdtsc sites in SCDA.
- The first build with it still misbehaved: cdb data breakpoints on
  `[0x5EADF8/FC]` showed the QPC start stored as 0xFFFFFFFF_FB32BEFA.
  `gen/recomp_types.h` is a stale copy (2026-09-23) of the runtime template
  that the generator does not refresh, and the gen dir came first in the
  include path, so `recomp_rdtsc` was implicitly declared `int` (hidden by
  `/w`) and sign-extended. Fix: `projects/scda/CMakeLists.txt` puts
  `templates/runtime` first. The stale copy is left in place (generated
  directory, not deleted without consent) -- it is otherwise identical.
- Crashes then became 0xC0000409 (fail-fast) with an empty minidump:
  `abort()`/CRT invalid-parameter bypass the unhandled-exception filter.
  `projects/scda/src/main.c` now logs a host backtrace for both
  (`[SCDA-FAILFAST]`); `apu_mmio_veh` reports undecodable APU accesses
  (`[APU-VEH]`) and, with `RECOMP_VEH_TRACE=1`, other first-chance AVs.
- Resolved backtrace of the assert `addr % 4 == 0`:
  `mcpx_apu_gp_write` <- `apu_hook_handle_mmio` <- `apu_mmio_veh` <-
  guest `sub_004B8950` <- `sub_004BB020` <- `sub_004BB790` (underrun
  path). `sub_004B8950` zero-fills a track buffer `[track+0x2C]` with
  `rep stosd`/`rep stosb`; in the failing runs that buffer lies in the APU
  GP window.

  Non-deterministic: some runs reach lipsyncxbox.umd, Menu.SS2,

## Update 345 (2026-09-26): Bink audio starvation = device threads pinned to the guest core

- Another agent's undocumented change (18:24-18:32), verified against code
  and `tools/kernel_audit/test_bridge_ordinals.py` (10/10):
  `g_kernel_dispatch_slot` and `g_icall_source` are `RECOMP_TLS` now.
- Instrumentation without regeneration: `recomp_lookup_manual()` returns
  wrappers for the indirectly-called Bink sound-object slots 0x004BD380
  (update/check), 0x004BD530 (Lock), 0x004BD670 (Commit) when
  `RECOMP_BINKSND_TRACE=1`; host ring of the track fields, dumped at the
  first `[obj+0x5C]` 0->1 (or at `RECOMP_BINKSND_DUMP_AT=N`).
- Track object (= Bink track struct, stride 0x17C): +0x7C DirectSound
  buffer, +0x84 size, +0x88 chunk, +0xA8 producer offset, +0xAC bytes to
  fill, +0xB4/+0xB8 last play/write cursor, +0xBC free-space threshold,
  +0xC0/+0xC4 last check time / limit. sub_004BD380 sets +0x5C ("ran dry")
  at 0x4BD4D7 when the check interval exceeds +0xC4 or free space >= +0xBC.
- xemu (`tools/debug/xemu_update345_binksnd.py`, one breakpoint to find
  the object, then halt/read/continue polling): producer stays 0x400-0x2000
  behind the write cursor, +0xAC stays 0, no starvation in 18 s. Geometry,
  thresholds and play rate identical to recomp.
- recomp: frames arrive every 100-120 ms (bursts of update calls every
  0.4 ms = Bink waiting for the next frame, then a long gap); one frame's
  audio per frame cannot cover 100+ ms of playback -> free space reaches the
  threshold after ~400 ms. Without `RECOMP_FB_WINDOW` the gaps are 33-70 ms
  and there is no starvation; `RECOMP_PB_EXEC` alone is harmless.
- Ruled out: fast play cursor, wrong size/rate, KeDelayExecutionThread
  granularity (<500 calls in 45 s, `RECOMP_DELAY_STATS`), framebuffer
  window CPU cost (0.2 ms per refresh, `RECOMP_FB_TIME`).
- Sampling profiler (`RECOMP_SAMPLE_MAIN=start,duration` in main.c;
  function buckets via RtlLookupFunctionEntry): main thread 67 % (no
  window) / 100 % (window) in `sub_004A12B0`, D3D's kick, which sets bit 16
  of NV2A PFB 0x100410 and spins until it clears. Only the NV2A ack thread
  clears it, and since 2026-09-11 the whole process was pinned to core 0,
  so the spinner kept the core for a full quantum first (longer for a
  foreground window's process).
- Fix: `xbox_PinGuestThread()` (main thread, `bridge_thread_main`,
  `xbox_thread_wrapper`) keeps guest threads on core 0 -- the 2026-09-11
  single-core semantics -- and `xbox_PinDeviceThread()` moves the NV2A ack,
  watchdog, APU frame, framebuffer window and FMV pump threads to the other
  cores, as the devices run concurrently on hardware.
- Build 2026-09-26 21:28:37, SHA-256
  `6de34b40d218eb1a4c9a4dbe3b1fefd3de64aa4ce24cb634a86ac7b73f62a3c6`:
  3/3 x 120 s with AC97+PB_EXEC+FB_WINDOW: no starvation, no crash, opens
  Menu.SS2, Menu_loading.bik, Menu_intro.bik. Framebuffer dumps: Ubisoft
  logo now full-screen (Bink block artefacts remain, separate issue), then
  the SCDA loading screen, static for >= 150 s (next blocker).
- Track audio pointers +0x28..+0x3C were normal guest RAM in all three
  starvation dumps, so the APU-window pointer of the old crash appears only
  inside the restart path; that path is no longer reached. Left open.

## Update 347b-d (2026-09-27): APU interrupts, DirectSound flush, HDD-cache install, main menu

- **Interrupt delivery.** DirectSound's ISR 0x004D2D0C (context = CMcpxAPU)
  services NV_PAPU_ISTS; bit 0x10 (FE trap) -> sub_004D2B53 -> FEDECMETH
  0x8000 (SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE) -> sub_004D25F8(voice), which clears the voice's
  0x8000 "stopping" flag via sub_004D4915 when [apu+0x84] == 0, the hw voice
  CFG_FMT lacks 0x800000, [apu+v*4+0x88] maps back to v and the voice's
  +0x4C list is non-empty. Kernel now delivers connected ISRs at the end of
  guest kernel calls (IRQL gate fs:[0x24], one ISR/DPC at a time, volatile
  guest registers saved); DPC queue for KeInsertQueueDpc/KeRemoveQueueDpc;
  KeSynchronizeExecution runs its routine at the interrupt IRQL. Kf*Irql
  fixed to fastcall (ecx) and to keep fs:[0x24].
- **Why the first version did not help:** the ISR ran (thousands of
  deliveries, `[APU-TRAP] ISR read ... FEDECMETH=0x8000 FEDECPARAM=74`) but
  against context 0x013790F4: DirectSound is created three times and
  disconnects its interrupt in between (KeDisconnectInterrupt, ordinal 100,
  was unbridged), so the first registration stuck. With disconnect bridged
  the flush completes (`[SCDA-BSOFF] returned, flags=0x0101`).
- **APU port gaps.** xemu's frame thread turns set_irq into update_irq each
  iteration; the port lacked it. Added. `[APU-TRAP]` logs (VOICE_OFF,
  SE2FE_IDLE_VOICE, PIO while trapped, ISR reads of FEDECMETH).
- **Install stalls at random chunk counts** (41, 77): not a deadlock but lock
  starvation -- `cdb -pv` snapshots at fixed times showed the main thread in
  voice_lock -> qemu_mutex_lock and the frame thread busy in se_frame ->
  voice_process. throttle() only waits every 8th frame and not at all when
  behind realtime, and a CRITICAL_SECTION is unfair. apu_lock_for_mmio
  counts waiting MMIO threads; the frame thread hands the lock over between
  frames (bounded 5 ms). Clean install then completes (84 x 2 MB reads,
  Summary.txt lists Stream.SS2, Fol_Common.SS2, deu\Stream.LS2,
  deu\SCX_Barks_Usa.LS2 with full sizes).
- **Result:** with a complete cache the flow START -> loading screen (video
  without bar) -> A -> main menu works (user-confirmed; A presses reach
  XInputGetState, packets 4-9 in run347z). Input: keyboard on port 0 when
  the framebuffer window has focus, XInput pads on ports 0-3;
  projects/scda/start_scda.bat sets the runtime variables.
- Log files: scratchpad run347t/u/v/w/x/y/z.log, snap347x_*.txt (starvation
  stacks), xemu347_bsoff2.log.

  sub_0003F514: XCalculateSignature over the file, append 20 bytes, compare
  size) -> 1; GetFileSize (+0x10, sub_00040FAC) -> 9804. So the save works;
  the load fails: sub_00294708 -> vtable+0x58 (sub_00042577) =
  XFindFirstSaveGame("U:\") (sub_00053DDA) -> XAPI FindFirstFile
  (sub_000528D1) never produced an entry.
- Causes: (1) NtQueryDirectoryFile takes 10 args on Xbox (FileInformationClass
  before FileMask; XAPI pushes 1); the bridge read 9 and cleaned 36 bytes, so
  FindFirstFile popped edi/esi 4 bytes low. (2) bridge_get_xbox_path ignored
  ANSI_STRING.Length; FindFirstFile's directory name is "U:\" inside a buffer
  holding "U:\*" -> NtOpenFile("U:\*") failed 0xC0000001. (3) NtClose (bridge
  used CloseHandle directly) never released the directory-enumeration context;
  also "." and ".." are filtered (FATX has none). (4) Exposed by the fixes:
  kernel_path mapped "\Device\Harddisk0\Partition5\" (trailing separator) to
  Partition5.img, whose directory redirect listed recomp_saves itself during
  SCDA's cache check; with a trailing separator partitions 1-5 now go through
  the rules table (Z: root = recomp_saves\Cache). Nothing was deleted (checked).
- Result (run348k, scripted input): cache check lists Default\DataXb\Sounds\...
  and Summary.txt; XFindFirstSaveGame enumerates six profile directories,
  reads each SaveMeta.xbx, then profile.sav of the chosen one. Open: a write to
  \Device\CdRom0\Default\cbf36687 (disp=5) right after.

## Update 349 (2026-09-27): title relaunch, interrupt-aware waits, mission-load crash, generator wrapper fix

- **Relaunch.** "New game" ends in HalReturnToFirmware(2) with a launch data
  page (path `\Device\CdRom0;default.xbe`, data 'scmo','pad1','sc3m','sc3p'):
  SCDA reboots itself into the mission (XLaunchNewImage). The kernel treated
  it as exit. Now bridge_relaunch_same_title writes the 4 KB page to
  launch_data.bin (exe dir), starts a new instance (same command line and
  environment) and exits; kernel_data_init -> bridge_load_launch_page puts
  the page into a fresh contiguous page and sets LaunchDataPage (164). main.c
  moves the old log to scda_runtime_prelaunch.log when launch_data.bin exists
  (in practice the child keeps writing to the same scda_runtime.log).
  User-confirmed: new window, mission loading bar, controls screen, intro video.
- **Deadlock with all threads waiting** (intro hang, freeze after skipping
  the mission video; log shows no kernel call at all afterwards): interrupts
  and DPCs were only delivered at the end of kernel calls. Blocking waits
  (KeWaitForSingleObject, NtWaitForSingleObject(Ex),
  NtWaitForMultipleObjectsEx, KeDelayExecutionThread) now wait in 4 ms slices
  (irq_aware_wait) and call xbox_irq_deliver in between; zero/absolute
  timeouts pass through. Menu flow re-checked by script (run349d).
- **Mission-load crash** (dumps 14-11-33 and 14-37-49): VCRUNTIME memmove
  with count 0xFFFFFFFC from sub_00367270 <- TArray::Remove sub_001C445D <-
  sub_00112276(index) <- sub_00112A5B <- sub_0008FB94 <- sub_00271F0C <-
  sub_001D2A4E. sub_00112276 removes one entry from five parallel arrays
  (+0x60/+0x6C/+0x84 byte, +0x78/+0x90 float); one float array is one entry
  short. Loops and add/insert/empty paths are symmetric (disassembly in this
  entry's session: 0x112A93 loop with dec edi, 0x112BC3 reverse loop,
  sub_00112425 adds to all five, sub_00112526/sub_00112692 empty all).
  Wrappers `[SCDA-FADE]` added around sub_00112276/sub_00112425/sub_00112A5B.
- **Generator bug:** wrapping renames the generated body to sub_X_gen via
  func_db, and `_call_target_name` then named every direct call site (and the
  dispatch entry) sub_X_gen, so wrappers never ran. Fixed: calls and dispatch

## Update 351 (2026-09-27): Missionslauf hing statt abzustuerzen -- CreateSuspended-Semantik in der Recomp-Thread-Bridge repariert

Der Lauf des 15:06-Builds blieb nach dem Missionsvideo aktiv, machte aber
keinen Fortschritt. CPU und Log waren stabil; ein CDB-Allthread-Snapshot
zeigte den Hauptthread in `sub_004BBD40`, wo er auf Bink-Pool-Worker TID 10896
wartete. Der Worker hing in `sub_004BBE90 -> sub_00052D2E ->
sub_00052C18 -> NtWaitForSingleObjectEx` auf dem nativen Handle `0x20`.
`!handle 20 f` klassifizierte es als leeres IoCompletion-Objekt. Der Wert ist
nicht getaggt und kommt in `s_handle_table` nicht vor.

Die optimierten Symbole plus Gaststack lokalisierten den Worker-Kontext auf
`0x01424C20`. Sein fertiger Zustand war plausibel (`state=3`, `+4=0x4C`,
`+8=0x4800000C`, Thread `+0x0C=0x4800000A`, Thread-ID `+0x10=0x50`, Mutant
`+0x14=0x4800000B`). Der Gaststack bei `sub_004BBEB1` enthielt dagegen
`handle=0x20`, Timeout `-1`. Nach dem kontrollierten Beenden des blockierten
Prozesses lieferte das vollstaendige Log den zeitlichen Beweis:

```
PsCreateSystemThreadEx #3 ... ctx2=0x01424C20
worker wait token=0x059DD910 ... finite -> STATUS_UNSUCCESSFUL
worker wait token=0x00000020 ... INFINITE
SCDA-DIAG234O/F spawned/token registration
NtCreateEvent ... real handle/token creation
```

Der Worker lief also vor Abschluss seiner eigenen Konstruktion und las zwei
stale Heap-Dwords als Synchronisationshandles. Das ist kein fehlender
Producer und kein IoCompletion-Bridgeproblem.

Die statische Kette erklaert die Absicht eindeutig. `sub_004BBF00` pusht den
Wert 4 zu `sub_00052572`; dieser Wrapper bildet daraus fuer
`PsCreateSystemThreadEx` `CreateSuspended = (value >> 2) & 1`, also 1. Erst
nach dem Create legt der Konstruktor Mutant (`sub_00052BA0`) und Event
(`sub_00052B01`) an. `sub_00052369 -> NtResumeThread` ist der spaetere,
bereits vorhandene Startpfad. Die native Referenzimplementierung in
`kernel_thread.c` respektiert CreateSuspended bereits, die fuer recompiled
Code tatsaechlich benutzte Sonderbruecke `bridge_PsCreateSystemThreadEx`
ignorierte Argument 7 jedoch und startete via `CreateThread(..., 0, ...)`
sofort.

Allgemeiner Fix in `src/kernel/kernel_bridge.c`: Argument 7 lesen, an
`bridge_spawn_thread` weitergeben und `CREATE_SUSPENDED` setzen. Kein
SCDA-spezifischer Patch, kein kuenstliches Signalisieren. Regressionstest
`test_spawned_threads_honor_create_suspended` zum Kernel-Audit hinzugefuegt.
Tests: Kernel-Audit 11/11, Wrapper 2/2, LAHF 4/4. Kanonischer Build
erfolgreich: `build/scda_upgrade/bin/RelWithDebInfo/scda_recomp.exe`,
2026-09-27 15:25:33, 96.985.600 Bytes, SHA-256
`CFBE11294485C95B6287A5018F252C2D64AE2CD88D14035505295549D5B16BAE`.
Runtime noch offen. Naechster Test ist derselbe interaktive Missionspfad;
das neue Log muss `suspended=1` zeigen und darf vor dem echten Resume keinen
untagged Bink-Worker-Wait mehr enthalten. Modellstufe STRONG/HIGH.
## Update 352 (2026-09-27): Missionsvideo-Crash ist eine zweite Form der rueckwaerts indizierten MSVC-memmove-Sprungtabelle -- erster Fade-Zustandsfehler bewiesen, allgemeiner Lifter-Fix regeneriert und gebaut

Der Nutzerlauf mit Build `CFBE1129...B16BAE` lief durch den vorherigen
Bink-Stillstand hindurch und erzeugte den gueltigen Dump
`SCDA_crash_2026-09-27_15-30-46.dmp`. Die `CreateSuspended`-Korrektur aus
Update 351 ist damit runtime-bestaetigt (`suspended=1`, kein alter Wait auf
das rohe Handle `0x20`).

Der Fade-Ring fand den ersten abweichenden Zustand, nicht nur den spaeteren
Crash: Objekt `0x010D8758` war nach dem ersten Add korrekt `1/1/1/1/1`; beim
zweiten `sub_00112425` wurde daraus `2/1/1/1/1`. Erst danach versuchte
`sub_00112276` Index 1 aus allen Listen zu entfernen und faultete. Der
ABI-Logger direkt davor meldete fuer den ersten Insert-Aufruf:

```
[ICALL] source=0x003672C4 target=0x003673D4 ...
[ABI] sub_000677DF: esi edi esp(epilogue never ran)
[ABI] sub_00122B58: esi edi
[ABI] sub_00141F12: esi edi
```

`sub_000677DF` ist ein Tail-Jump auf `sub_00367270`, MSVCs `memmove`.
Original-x86 bei `0x003672AC` zieht fuer kleine Kopien 4 von der Laenge ab;
bei 0..3 Bytes ist ECX daher -4..-1. Der Jump
`jmp dword ptr [ecx*4 + 0x003673CC]` liest seine vier Ziele folglich bei
`0x003673BC..0x003673C8`, komplett vor dem Displacement. Das Displacement
selbst zeigt bereits auf den ersten Epilog. Der Lifter kannte seit Update 333
Rueckwaerts-Tabellen, brach in `_analyze_switch_table()` aber bei einer
vollstaendig leeren Vorwaertslesung ab. So blieb gerade diese Variante ein
`RECOMP_ITAIL`; der allgemeine Dispatcher rief den falsch als Funktion
klassifizierten internen Block `sub_003673D4` auf. Dessen Epilog bezog sich
nicht mehr auf den aktiven memmove-Frame, wodurch ESI/EDI/ESP beschaedigt
wurden und `sub_00112425` nach dem ersten Array nicht mehr korrekt fortfuhr.

Die allgemeine Reparatur in `tools/recomp/lifter.py` entfernt nur diesen
vorzeitigen Abbruch und probiert `_read_jump_table_below()` auch bei null
Vorwaertseintraegen. Der neue Test
`test_table_entirely_below_displacement_becomes_a_switch` modelliert exakt
die vier Slots unterhalb von Code am Displacement. Gezielte Tests 4/4,
gesamte `tools/recomp`-Suite 108/108. Vollstaendige Regeneration mit dem
kanonischen `scda_v060`-Befehl: 32.102/32.111 Funktionen, 0 Fehler. Die
generierte Stelle `loc_003672C4` ist nun ein Vier-Ziel-Switch mit lokalen
Gotos nach `0x003673CC/D4/E0/F4`; kein Dispatcher-/Funktionswechsel mehr.

scheiterte wie bekannt an MSBuild FileTracker E_ACCESSDENIED, der

  and `test al,dl`) joining at `setne al`; translator only merged equal

  ((a-b)&mask or a&b); `_merge_flag_states` yields ("zres", []) for mixed
  cmp/test joins; `_make_condition` resolves je/jne (and thus sete/setne/
  cmove/cmovne) from `_fzr`. Test tools/recomp/test_flag_merge_zres.py (4),
  suite 113/113. Regenerated. 393 `_flags` conditions and 13 setcc remain

## Update 354 (2026-09-27) -- float-compare joins; level no longer freezes

- User report: in-level message box, then nothing reacts (START/SELECT
  too). run353u log: GPU counters frozen at 1269 draws after the message
  box -> the title stalled; run354b: crash (abort, apu_dsp.c:392 assert)
  after wild ICALLs/NULLVCALLs. Both preceded by corrupt objects (vtable
  slot = code bytes 0x8BC1940F, one-byte-shifted pointer 0x5B57F80D) --
  first wild calls differ per run, so looked for bad control flow.
- Classified the remaining `_flags` fallbacks (scratchpad flagscan.py).
  Real-code classes: (a) comiss/fcomi compares whose consumer sits behind a
  label joined by another float compare with different operands (e.g.
  0x0008C215/0x0008C233 -> jbe at 0x0008C240, always false); (b) joins of
  result setters on one destination (`and ebx,m` / `inc ebx` -> je at
  0x0030A4F5); (c) fragment "functions" starting with a jcc (seeded from
  data refs, e.g. 0x00011DBD) -- left alone.
- Fix: comiss family lifts to `g_fp_cmp = RECOMP_FCMP(a, b)`; conditions
  for all float compares come from g_fp_cmp, NaN-correct
  (`_fp_cmp_condition`); `_flag_states_agree` treats any two float compares
  as equal; x87 fcom/ftst drop a tracked float-flag state (they rewrite
  g_fp_cmp but not EFLAGS). New join state "zsres" (ZF/SF from a shared
  destination) for add/sub/and/or/xor/inc/dec/neg/adc/sbb. Result-setter SF
  now uses the operand width. Fallbacks 408 -> 373. Tests
  tools/recomp/test_fp_cmp_join.py (8); suite 121/121. Regenerated, built
  18:43:54, SHA c87c7ac9...45d2.
- run354c (script, 330 s): level keeps running -- draws 53,261, 22.9M
  indices and still rising, no freeze, no crash. Framebuffer black: GPU
  report shows 43,391 batches with unsupported pixel programs, 845
  textured, mostly rendering into a 512x512 target. Late wild ICALLs at
  0x0029D0E5 / 0x002A243D remain.
- XAudio2 output initialises; silence must come from the APU/DSP side.
- Decision: the CPU bring-up rasterizer cannot carry in-level graphics;
  next big step is porting xemu's OpenGL PGRAPH renderer (local source
  SC4_xbe_hack/third_party/xemu_0_8_66_source) with a small WGL loader.

## Renderer decision (2026-09-27, user decision, binding for later agents)

- TARGET RENDERER: **OpenGL**, ported from xemu's GL PGRAPH backend
  (SC4_xbe_hack/third_party/xemu_0_8_66_source/hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/gl +
  glsl/*, pgraph.c, texture.c, swizzle.c, s3tc.c). Chosen by the user because
  it is simpler to port and debug than Vulkan. Linux is not a reason against
  it (Mesa supports GL well).
- Vulkan (xemu pgraph/vk) is explicitly deferred: it would need Vulkan
  headers + glslang downloads (only VMA and SPIRV-Reflect are local) and
  ~10k more lines. The GLSL shader generators (glsl/psh.c, vsh*.c) are
  shared with a later Vulkan backend, so keep that layer backend-neutral.
- No downloads needed for GL: use opengl32 + WGL with a small in-tree
  function loader instead of libepoxy/SDL.
- The CPU bring-up rasterizer in src/kernel/nv2a_pb_exec.c stays as the
  fallback until the GL renderer draws the menu correctly.


## Update 355 (2026-09-27) -- xemu OpenGL NV2A attached; AC97 controller, guest KEVENTs, loop flag fixpoint

Renderer port per the OpenGL decision above. `src/gpu/` holds xemu 0.8.66
(HEAD 8667193001e) pfifo/pgraph/gl/glsl plus shims, a WGL loader and the
glue `nv2a_recomp.c`, enabled by `RECOMP_NV2A_XEMU=1` (old CPU rasterizer
stays default). Aperture 0xFD000000 is PAGE_NOACCESS and decoded by
`src/kernel/mmio_decode.c`; IRQ 3 via xbox_irq_set_line; 59.94 Hz VBlank
thread; scanout surface downloaded to guest RAM for the FB window.

Blockers fixed on the way to a visible menu (all proven by run logs /
cdb snapshots in the session scratchpad, runs 355d..356e):

1. Pushbuffer entry: D3D writes the entry jump through VA 0x80000000 and
   starts at GET=0; the first 64 KiB there are now a view of physical 0.
2. Interrupt delivery: after trapped register accesses
   (xbox_irq_deliver_from_mmio) and via an asynchronous injector that
   hijacks a guest thread executing generated code (RtlRestoreContext);
   the parallel agent added a per-basic-block safepoint and level
   re-sampling with line generations.
3. AC97 (0xFEC00000): DirectSound sub_004D88ED writes CR_RR to the PCM-out
   bus master and spins on `test cl,cl / jne $-2` over the read-back value
   (real XBE bytes 0x4D891A..0x4D8925). Hardware/xemu clear RR during the
   reset; plain memory kept it, and the spin at DISPATCH_LEVEL also blocked
   the D3D DPC. Build 354c only passed because MSVC deleted the side-effect
   free infinite loop; with the safepoint call the loop is kept, so the old
   path hung too. `src/kernel/mcpx_aci.c` ports xemu ac97.c/aci.c register
   semantics (mixer, bus masters, GLOB_STA codec-ready, IRQ 6, PCM-out DMA
   paced at 48 kHz with samples discarded) and replaces the plain-memory
   codec-ready poke under RECOMP_AC97_READY.
4. Guest KEVENTs: D3D waits `while (KeWaitForSingleObject(&ev,6,1,0,NULL));`
   (0x4A15D8, ev = 0x004AD43C) for the event its DPC sets with KeSetEvent
   (0x4A342E). The kernel treated the pointer as a Win32 HANDLE: the wait
   failed immediately (~4 M calls/s), the set was lost. kernel_bridge.c now
   recognises an NT-initialised KEVENT in guest memory (Type 0/1, Size 4,
   empty wait list), keeps SignalState there and waits on a generation
   counter with IRQ/DPC delivery between 4 ms slices.
5. Lifter: loop heads lost the flags of their back edge (address-order walk)
   and fell to the always-false `_flags`. zlib pqdownheap sub_0004ED7F
   (`jge` 0x4EDA2) then compared past the heap end; gen_bitlen wrote through
   a wild index into the NV2A aperture while compressing
   AutoSave.sav.tmp.z, which xemu's user.c asserts on. translator.py solves
   block flag states to a fixpoint (`_solve_block_flag_states`, only for
   functions with back edges); tests test_loop_flag_fixpoint.py; suite
   124/124; `_flags` fallbacks 361 -> 335.

Result (build 2026-09-27 21:54:32, SHA-256 bb5982fb...d62d38): title
screen, main menu and profile menu render with real textures and readable
German text; profile save no longer crashes; New Game relaunches the title.
Open: after the relaunch the level load shows a black screen and frames
advance only sporadically (main thread in sub_0029CA11); scattered noise

## Update 356 (2026-09-28) -- level playable: sqrt, packed SSE, rounding; display path; save diagnosis

All proven with runtime evidence (cdb snapshots of the user's process,
guest-stack dumps, save traces; logs in the session scratchpad):

1. appSqrt (sub_00067AB9) = x*rsqrtss(x) masked by `cmpneqss 0, x`; the
   lifter emitted cmpneqss as a TODO comment, the mask stayed 0 and every
   square root returned 0. Symptom: line-check end point (-inf,-inf,-inf)
   (frame at 0xF786C8 in sub_0029CA11), each check walked the whole
   16384-cell grid -> one frame per ~35 s after the first cutscene. Fix:
   scalar SSE compares cmp{eq,lt,le,unord,neq,nlt,nle,ord}{ss,sd} and the
   cmpss/cmpsd imm form (`_scalar_cmp_predicate`, NaN-correct, low lane).
2. sqrtps/rsqrtps/rcpps computed the low lane only (232 sites): now
   XMM_SQRT/XMM_RSQRT/XMM_RCP over four lanes. Result: player model and
   weapon render (were invisible / camera-fade by wrong distances).
3. Rounding: cvtss2si/cvtsd2si were a truncating C cast (now MXCSR
   rounding via _mm_cvtss_si32); ldmxcsr/stmxcsr map to the host MXCSR
   (RC/FTZ/DAZ, exceptions masked); fist/fistp/frndint honour the x87 RC
   bits of g_fp_control_word. Title Bink video visibly cleaner.
4. Display: the window now takes the scan-out like xemu's UI
